name: Bacuri butter
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Bacuri butter is obtained by cold pressing the fruit seeds. Each fruit contains up to four
seeds which would yield, after drying, up to 70% oil. Traditionally, the fruits are soaked in
water (up to one year) and then boiled in water. The fat floats on top of the water and is
then separated. In the modern, industrial method, the fruits are cold-pressed and physically
filtered afterwards to separate shells and other impurities.

Bacuri butter is an emollient that provides lasting hydration for the skin with skin smoothing
and anti-ageing properties to help stabilise collagen and elastin production.

It is easily absorbed and has nourishing properties. Bacuri butter can be used in hair and
scalp hair products and skincare, where it enhances skin radiance. It can be used raw,
directly on the skin.

Clinical trials conducted by manufacturers have suggested the efficacy of bacuri butter
on improving the skin’s barrier integrity, along with its ability to reduce transepidermal
water loss.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Lip care, haircare, body and skincare such as anhydrous creams, balms, butters, scrubs, and
emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
To avoid graininess in your butter blends, follow the recommended formulation method
outlined in the course.

name: Cocoa butter
function: Emollient, fragrance, skin conditioning, skin protecting
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Cupuaçu butter comes from the cupuaçu fruit tree, which belongs to the cocoa family.
It is native to the northern Amazon.

Cupuaçu butter is an excellent moisturiser with good water absorption properties. It can
absorb approximately 200% more water than lanolin, which makes it a modern, plant-based
alternative to this emollient. It can help stabilise emulsions.

Cupuaçu butter is also rich in antioxidants and phytosterols – more notably beta-sitosterol,
which has anti-inflammatory properties and helps to improve the skin’s lipid barrier.

This butter penetrates the skin quickly whilst retaining moisture and effectively preventing
transepidermal water loss (TEWL) – the evaporation of skin’s water content.

It can help improve the appearance of prematurely ageing skin and has excellent anti-
inflammatory and emollient properties that promote skin elasticity and improve hydration.

This butter is very similar to cocoa butter and can be used as a substitute. It can be
included in formulations at a high concentration, as it has a creamy texture and is a great
emollient that provides a softening effect on the skin.

It also has interesting properties when added to haircare and cleansing products, targeted
towards preventing dehydration and improving mechanical resistance and elasticity of
the hair.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Lip care, haircare, body, and skincare such as anhydrous creams, balms, butters, scrubs,
and emulsions. Use it in massage products where its spreadability is wanted. It is also an
excellent choice for hair conditioners and hair masks.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
To avoid graininess in your butter blends, follow the recommended formulation method
outlined in the course.

name: Illipe butter
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Illipe butter is a vegetable fat derived from the nut of the Shorea stenoptera tree, found in
the rainforests of Southeast Asia. Its traditional use in medicine, food, and skincare makes
the tree an important botanical in its native region.

The fatty acids in illipe butter are fairly resistant to heat and oxidation, which is great news
for formulators. It resembles cocoa butter, but with a slightly higher melting point. If you are
not fond of the aroma associated with cocoa butter, substitute it with illipe butter in solid
balm lotions.

Illipe butter is a soothing emollient ingredient that helps to protect the skin barrier function
and has long-lasting moisturisation properties. It is widely used for its skin-softening
qualities and can replace synthetic emollients in hair and scalp care products.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Lip care, haircare, body, and skincare such as anhydrous creams, balms, butters, scrubs,
and emulsions. Use it in hair masks and hair conditioners, or in any product where a hard
butter is required.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
To avoid graininess in your butter blends, follow the recommended formulation method
outlined in the course.

name: Kombo butter
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Kombo butter, also known as African nutmeg, possesses anti-inflammatory and antifungal
properties. It has some antioxidant activity due to its content of kombic acid, helping to
delay the rancidity of other oils used in combination with it.

It is known as a dry butter with a dark brown colour. It is thick, grainy, and buttery.
Kombo butter is an interesting choice to use in formulations aimed at dry skin or in
massage products.

Kombo butter, as well as its acid extract and each of the three pure compounds isolated
from it (sargacquinoic acid, sargachromenol, and sargahydroquinoic acid), possess
significant antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities. Some in vitro studies even
demonstrated that sargaquinoic acid could improve the appearance of hyperpigmentation.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Lip care, haircare, body, and skincare such as anhydrous creams, balms, butters, scrubs,
and emulsions. Use it in massage products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
To avoid graininess in your butter blends, follow the recommended formulation method
outlined in the course.

Kombo butter has a very strong colour, so think about this when adding it to formulations.

name: Kpangnan butter
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
This butter is extracted from the seeds of the berries that grow on the kpangnan tree. The
tree is native to Africa and grows in dense forests and riverbanks.

It is rich in tocopherols, mainly beta-tocopherol, and has shown good stability to oxidation.
Due to its high content of stigmasterol, this silky non-oily butter is known for its soothing
and anti-inflammatory properties.

This butter can be used on its own in formulations or can be blended with others. It is a
great ingredient in lip balms and lotion bars to give an occlusive layer. Use it in haircare
products, like masks or styling products. It has good emollient properties and is often used
in products to help restore skin elasticity. It is a solid butter that melts at room temperature.
The butter gives a natural shine to dry, damaged hair when used in haircare products.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Lip care, haircare, body and skincare such as anhydrous creams, balms, butters, scrubs, and
emulsions. Can be used in massage body bars.

Kpangnan is sometimes mislabelled and sold as “golden shea butter” or “yellow shea
butter” although they are completely different species.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
To avoid graininess in your butter blends, follow the recommended formulation method
outlined in the course.

name: Mafura butter
heatStability: Good, but not recommended to heat above 50 °C
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Mafura butter is cold-pressed from the seeds of the mafura tree, sometimes called Natal
Mahogany. A single tree yields on average around 20 litres of oil. It is well-known across
Southern Africa for its cosmetic properties.

The butter is solid at room temperature and melts at 30 °C (86 °F) (do not heat higher than 50 °C (122 °F)).
Like shea butter, mafura has a high content of oleic acid that gives it a softer consistency
than most butters.

It has a smooth and creamy texture and is a great emollient that nourishes and revitalises
the skin. Mafura butter has a non-greasy feel and is easy to spread, so try it in products
designed for body massage. It is also often used in haircare products and works well with
coconut oil in soaps.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Lip care, haircare, body and skincare such as anhydrous creams, balms, butters, scrubs, and
emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
To avoid graininess in your butter blends, follow the recommended formulation method
outlined in the course.

• References: African seed oils of commercial importance — Cosmetic applications

                                         BUTTERS:

name: Mango butter
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Mango butter is extracted from the large seed at the heart of the mango fruit. It is harder
than butters like shea, making it an ideal additive in formulas of thicker creams, especially
when paired with cocoa butter.

It is a semi-soft butter that melts on contact with skin. It is commonly known as a dry butter,
meaning it absorbs into the skin comparatively faster than other plant butters.

Mango butter has an aesthetically pleasing white colour, which works well to give a
‘commercial’ look to your skincare products.

Mango butter is an excellent emollient and has been reported to reduce wrinkles and other
signs of ageing. It is also rich in vitamin E and has a long shelf life due to its high amounts
of unsaponifiable matter.

Mango butter has antioxidant and rejuvenating activities, which can help restore the
impaired barrier function of the skin.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Lip care, haircare, body, and skincare such as anhydrous creams, balms, butters, scrubs,
and emulsions. Being a butter that we call dry butter, it works best when blended with the
softer and richer fats and oils such as shea.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
To avoid graininess in your butter blends, follow the recommended formulation method
outlined in the course.

• References: Mango butter in cosmetic formulations.

                                         BUTTERS:

name: Murumuru butter
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Murumuru butter is a great emollient that promotes skin suppleness, especially for dry,
cracked, and acne-prone skin. It has excellent moisturising properties, thanks to its unusual
content of glycerol.

It gives a natural gloss to dry and damaged hair, protecting the fibers against physical
damage from brushing and combing.

This butter is similar in composition to coconut oil, but it is harder. It has some antioxidant
activity that might help delay the rancidity of other oils used in combination with it.

You can use it in any product designed for skin repair.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Lip care, haircare, body, and skincare such as anhydrous creams, balms, butters, scrubs,
and emulsions. Try it in after-sun products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
To avoid graininess in your butter blends, follow the recommended formulation method
outlined in the course.

• References: Amazon oil – Murumuru Butter.

                                         BUTTERS:

name: Shea butter
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Shea butter is extracted from shea nuts from the karite tree, which grows in Ghana. Shea
butter is known for its luxurious moisturising properties. It is important to note that shea
butter does not possess an SPF factor and therefore is not suitable for use as sunscreen.

The extraction of the butter begins by boiling the nuts in water, then grinding them into
a paste until the oils start to separate. This work is traditionally done over an open fire
by women.

Shea butter melts at body temperature and is easily absorbed into the outermost layers of
the skin. It is rich in oleic acid and has a soft consistency, unusual in vegetable butters. This
butter can feel rich and greasy for some. You can, however, change the skin feel by blending
it with butters such as mango, which is what we call dry butter. In general, it combines well
with other butters.

It also has a strong aroma unless you use the refined version, which we don’t recommend
as the refining process can remove some beneficial properties.

Shea butter is considered a great choice for dry and irritated skin and skin that has a
disrupted barrier function. This is not only because of its nourishing ratio of fatty acids,
but also due to its high content of unsaponifiable matter.

It has been well-documented to improve the appearance of scars and stretch marks, and
it can also be used without processing as a protective lip balm. In vitro and in vivo studies
demonstrated its anti-inflammatory properties.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Lip care, haircare, body, and skincare such as anhydrous creams, balms, butters, scrubs,
and emulsions, especially those designed for dry skin or hair.

When using it in formulations, it is not necessary to melt it as it can be whipped with a
whisk until creamy, then blended with oils or other melted fats.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Shea is prone to graininess, so following the recommended formulation method outlined
in the course will help overcome this problem.

• References: How to Make a Body Butter.

                                         BUTTERS:

name: Tucuma butter
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Tucuma butter comes from the tucuma palm tree, native to the Amazonian rainforest.
This tree is from the same family as the murumuru palm, and these butters have similar
properties. Both butters are used as silicone replacements in formulations, forming a
protective layer on the skin and hair.

It is a solid butter that melts at room temperature and can be used on its own in
formulations or blended with other butters. It is a great ingredient in lip balms and body
balm bars to provide an occlusive layer.

It has great emollient properties and is often used in products to help restore skin elasticity.
The butter also gives a natural shine to dry, damaged hair when used in haircare, in products
such as masks or styling formulations.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Lip care, haircare, body, and skincare such as anhydrous creams, balms, butters, scrubs,
and emulsions. Use it in hair masks and hair conditioners, in products designed to combat
cellulite and stretch marks.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
To avoid graininess in your butter blends, follow the recommended formulation method
outlined in the course.

name: Ucuuba butter
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Açai berries are gathered by hand from protected regions of the Amazon rainforest and then
cold-pressed to yield the freshest, purest oil possible. Açai oil is liquid at room temperature.
Due to its high palmitic acid content, it is considered a substitute for vegetable butters.
However, it provides a more pleasant, lighter, non-oily feeling to the skin.

Açai oil contains anthocyanins, phytosterols, and essential fatty acids. Its phytosterol
content includes beta-sitosterol, stigmasterol, and campesterol. These compounds help
stimulate cellular metabolism and reduce inflammation, as well as helping to improve the
skin lipid barrier. The anthocyanins, present in high amounts, are responsible for the oil
colour and antioxidant properties.

This oil has excellent thermal and oxidation stability, as it doesn't present significant
changes after short term heating and long-term storage. This means you can apply the oil in
cosmetics that need to be heated for a short period (such as hot process emulsions). Açai
oil is good for anti-ageing cosmetic products and creates green facial serums/oils.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Anhydrous products, facial or body oils, balms and all types of emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects known. No formulation restriction known.

name: Apricot kernel oil
substitution: Peach or plum oil, sweet almond oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Apricot kernel oil is cold-pressed from the seeds of apricot (Prunus armeniaca) or extracted
using solvents. We always recommend that you try to work with the cold-pressed version.

It is a light and nourishing oil, which is quickly absorbed by the skin. It soothes sensitive
skin can be used by people of all skin types.

The fatty acid composition of apricot kernel oil is similar to that of sweet almond oil,
meaning it is a good alternative for people with nut allergies. Much like almond oil, it has
softening and moisturising properties for the skin and hair. However, apricot kernel oil is
more expensive than almond oil.

Apricot kernel oil also contains phytosterols, tocopherols, and beta-carotene. Due to its
polyphenols content, it helps improve skin elasticity and tone while diminishing the signs of
ageing.

Thanks to its versatility, apricot kernel oil suits many different cosmetic purposes. It is
especially useful as an emollient ingredient in products for skin and hair.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Lip balms, haircare, anhydrous creams, balms, butters, scrubs, and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects known. No formulation restriction known.

name: Argan oil
colour: Copper colour / Virgin Argan oil is golden-coloured
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Argan oil is extracted from the nuts of the argan tree (Argania spinosa). The argan tree's
fruit is green and resembles an olive, but is larger. Inside, there is a hard-shelled nut that
contains up to three kernels, from which the argan oil is then extracted. The traditional
production of this oil is time-consuming and demanding: it takes about 100 kg of fruits to
make just 2-3 litres of oil.

Argan oil has been a big hit on the cosmetics scene over the last few years, especially in
hair products. Traditionally, argan oil was used in Morocco as a topical oil to prevent early
signs of ageing and help with dry skin conditions, inflammation, and acne. It is also valuable
to prevent hair loss and moisturise dry hair.

It contains linoleic acid, an omega-6 fatty acid, which helps improve skin elasticity in mature
skin. Also, argan oil contains some interesting compounds in its unsaponifiable matter.
It has a high tocopherol content and also contains sterols, carotenoids, and phenolic
compounds. These actives are responsible for this oil's antioxidant and anti-inflammatory
properties.

Argan oil is quickly absorbed and is often used in products directed to mature skin. It also
helps improve the appearance of oily skin, reducing greasiness when used in moderation. It
can be mixed with jojoba oil for daily use, or blended with rosehip and evening primrose for
a rejuvenating facial oil.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Soothing products, rejuvenating products especially for the face and neck area, and in
products aimed at problem skin. It is also excellent in haircare products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Argan oil is frequently adulterated, so purchase from trusted suppliers.

name: Avocado oil
oxidationStability: Good, but relatively short shelf life (1 year)
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Traditionally, Mexicans and South Americans have used the mashed fruit pulp to nourish
the skin and hair. Indeed, avocado oil is extracted from the fruit, not the seeds. The avocado
pulp usually contains around 15-40% oil, but the extraction must happen when the pulp is
dried out. Otherwise, it would emulsify.

Avocado oil is an option for a nut-free carrier oil. It is an oil that glides well on the skin,
making it an interesting choice for massage oils.

This oil has a high chlorophyll content, responsible for its bright green colour. Because of
chlorophyll’s propensity to photo-oxidise when exposed to light and oxygen, avocado oil is
quite unstable, so it needs to be kept in a cool, dark place.

Avocado also has a high content of palmitoleic acid and a combination of palmitic, linoleic
and oleic acids, making it a good choice for the care of damaged hair and skin. It has anti-
inflammatory and moisturising properties.

It also presents repairing properties related to the high amount of phytosterols present in
the oil. Beta-sitosterol, lutein, and vitamin E are three of the most significant lipid-soluble
compounds in avocado oil that present beneficial effects on the skin.

Laboratory in vivo research has demonstrated that avocado oil can help improve the
recovery of skin injuries by promoting increased synthesis of collagen and reducing the
inflammatory response.

It is an interesting choice for after-sun products, especially when blended with calendula
macerate and rosehip oil. It is a beneficial oil for dry, damaged, dehydrated and mature skin.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Emulsions, massage oils, lip gloss and lip balm, nighttime products, scrubs with oil/
anhydrous base.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects known. No formulation restriction known.

name: Babassu oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Babassu oil is a clear, light yellow vegetable oil that is solid at room temperature. It comes
from the fatty seeds of the babassu palm, a tree native to the Amazon rainforest.

Mainly composed of lauric and myristic acids, this oil has a melting point close to our body
temperature, which means that it melts on contact, just like coconut oil. In fact, babassu
and coconut share a similar fatty acid composition, meaning one can substitute the other.
However, babassu oil does not present as intense an aroma as coconut oil.

Lauric acid, one of the main components of babassu oil, is able to penetrate the hair shaft,
which results in less protein loss and increased mechanical resistance to physical damage
(brushing, combing, etc).

Studies suggest that babassu oil has wound healing and anti-inflammatory properties. It is
an excellent addition to any product designed for nourishing the skin and treating the hair
and scalp.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
It can be used to substitute coconut oil. Use it in body butters and body balms, it can also
be added to lip balms and emulsions. It is excellent in haircare products as well.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects known. No formulation restriction known.

name: Baobab oil
colour: A slightly thick oil with a golden yellow colour
substitution: Unique, but its closest substitute could be oat oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Baobab oil is extracted from the seeds of the Adansonia digitata tree. It is one of the most
prominent oils from Africa. The tree is very unusual as it looks like it is growing roots
upwards, which is why it is often called the upside-down tree.

Baobab oil is thick and is considered a liquid substitute for plant butters due to its high
amount of palmitic acid. However, it provides a lighter skin feel than vegetable butters.

This oil contains high amounts of unsaturated fatty acids, balanced by saturated fatty
acids. Because it is an emollient and a slightly occlusive oil, it helps improve the skin
barrier function, reducing the TEWL (transepidermal water loss) that occurs as a result of
an impaired barrier. It also helps increase the skin's elasticity and is recommended for dry,
damaged, or mature skin. Due to its linoleic acid content, it can also be applied to acne-
prone and oily skin.

Baobab oil also contains vitamins A and E, and phytosterols such as avenasterol,
campesterol, and beta-sitosterol, which provide anti-inflammatory properties

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in massage oils, and in products designed for stretch marks. It is often used in lip
care products, and recently is gaining popularity in haircare formulations as well. It is great
in scalp conditioning, and it leaves the hair silky and nourished.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects known. No formulation restriction known.

name: Borage seed oil
scent: A distinctive oily smell, sometimes considered unpleasant
substitution: Evening primrose or blackcurrant oils are good substitutes, but they contain alpha-linoleic acid (unlike borage oil) and significantly less gamma- linolenic acid
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Borage seed oil is extracted from the seeds of the Borago officinalis plant, also known as
starflower. The borage plant produces many tiny black seeds, which are cold-pressed to
create this oil.

Borage seed oil is liquid at room temperature and is very sensitive to heat.

Borage seed oil is the richest known source of gamma-linolenic acid (GLA), containing
around 18-25% GLA. It also contains high amounts of linoleic acid.

Borage seed oil also contains in its unsaponifiable fraction vitamin E (mainly gamma and
delta-tocopherol), squalene, and phytosterols like avenasterol, campesterol, and beta-
sitosterol. These phytosterols provide anti-inflammatory properties. In fact, evidence
suggests that borage seed oil can help in dry skin conditions, rebalancing the skin's lipid
and repairing the barrier function.

Often praised as one of the best plant oils to be used on sensitive skin, borage seed oil
helps to calm inflamed and irritated skin. It can also be used in products directed to
acne-prone and dry skin. It is a great emollient that helps improve the skin's suppleness
and elasticity.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in creams and anhydrous products designed to moisturise and help repair the skin
barrier. Great in products for dry and sensitive skin.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Borage seed oil is a sensitive oil, so you should only use it once your formula is under 40 °C (104 °F).
If you are making emulsions, it should be added during the cool down phase.

name: Brazil nut oil
restrictions: Caution for people with nut allergies
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Brazil nuts are seeds that grow in the South American rainforests. They grow inside a hard,
woody shell that needs to be broken. Brazil nut oil is cold-pressed from these oily seeds.
The seeds possess approximately 70% oil and contain high amounts of selenium.

Brazil nut oil contains vitamins A and E and squalene. It also has a high content of
phytosterols, which present a similar composition to olive and almond oils. Its main
phytosterols are beta-sitosterol, stigmasterol, and campesterol. Since these compounds
provide anti-inflammatory properties, Brazil nut oil is excellent in products directed to dry
and irritated skin.

It is a nourishing oil that is absorbed quickly by the skin. As it contains essential fatty acids
and is a great emollient, reducing the TEWL (transepidermal water loss), it can be used in
products for mature skin.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in creams and anhydrous products designed to moisturise, especially in products
for dry skin. It is also used in products for damaged and dehydrated hair, where it makes
a good combination with broccoli seed oil. Try it in aftershave products and lip balms. It is
also a good addition to problem skin formulations.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Individuals with nut allergies should be careful about using this oil.

name: Buriti oil
substitution: Olive oil, but it does not share the exact same properties
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Buriti oil is extracted from the fruit pulp of the moriche palm tree, native to the Amazon
rainforest. It is also called moriche palm oil.

This oil is considered one of the richest natural sources of beta-carotene, even more than
carrot oil. This is the reason this oil presents such an intense orange colour. Beware that it
can stain cloth and porous surfaces. Fortunately, it does not pass its colour to the skin.

Buriti oil also contains oleic acid, linoleic acid, palmitic acid, and tocopherols (vitamin
E). Because of its high levels of antioxidants, it is a good choice for products directed
to mature skin. It can help increase the skin's elasticity and improve the process of skin-
renewing. It also helps improve the appearance of scars.

As a matter of fact, an in vitro study researched the photoprotective effects of buriti oil. It
demonstrated that when cells were treated with buriti oil and its emulsions after ultraviolet
irradiation, photoprotective effects could be observed, reducing the damage caused by UV
light.

Buriti oil is an excellent choice for products aimed at mature skin or after sun exposure. You
can use it in creams, lotions, or even in lip or facial balms.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in emulsions and anhydrous products, balms and lip balms. It is useful in after-sun
products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It has a strong orange colour that can stain cloth and porous surfaces.

name: Camellia seed oil
inci: Camellia Japonica Seed Oil or Camellia Oleifera Seed Oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Camellia oil comes from a shrub that is the source of this edible oil. It is also known as
tea seed oil because it comes from a plant used to produce tea all over the world. Do not
confuse it with tea tree oil. The blossoming camellia tree is very beautiful. Tea oil has been
used in skin and haircare in China for centuries.

Camellia japonica oil is also known as tsubaki (dongbaek) oil. It possesses a variety of
biological activities, including antibacterial, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activity.

This oil is highly nutritious and similar to jojoba oil – it penetrates quickly into the skin
and doesn’t leave a greasy feel. It is used in skincare as an emollient that reduces
transepidermal water loss (TEWL) and soothes the skin, helping to restore skin elasticity.

You can use it in products for problem skin and formulations designed for dull skin. It is
equally useful in anti-ageing products, thanks to its antioxidant properties.

Tea oil triglycerides are rich sources of oleic acid, giving this oil some excellent skin and
hair-conditioning properties. A study has also shown that this oil has promising effects on
collagen, increasing the production of type-1 procollagen and decreasing its degradation.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Lip balms, haircare, nail care, anhydrous creams, balms, butters, scrubs, and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Do not confuse it with Camellia sinensis!

name: Castor oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Castor oil is obtained through the cold-pressing of the seeds of the castor plant and is
unique due to its high viscosity and slow absorption.

This oil contains about 90% ricinoleic acid, an omega-9 unsaturated fatty acid, which is
responsible for castor oil’s anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and moisturising properties.
The chemical structure of ricinoleic acid makes it more polar than other fatty acids,
providing humectant properties to this oil. Castor oil also contains small amounts of
phytosterols and vitamin E.

Castor oil has good emollient and lubricating properties, and it also presents an excellent
ability to wet and disperse pigments. It sticks well to the skin but spreads poorly, staying
in the application area. This characteristic is very important in highly pigmented decorative
cosmetics. This oil provides shine and lubrication to makeup products such as lipsticks, lip
gloss, and eye mascaras.

As a rich emollient and humectant oil, it can also be used in cleansers, shampoos,
conditioners, and moisturisers. It is excellent in makeup removers. Even if its use can go up
to 100%, its viscosity hinders its use as a standalone ingredient.

Although castor beans contain toxins such as ricin and ricinine, these are not extracted into
the oil and remain in the leftovers of the oil production.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Lip balms, lip gloss, haircare, anhydrous creams, balms, butters, scrubs, and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects known. No formulation restriction known.

name: Coconut oil
function: Skin conditioning, hair conditioning, fragrance, perfuming
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Coconut oil is cold-pressed from dried coconut fruit pulp and melts at around 25ºC, which
is why it is liquid in hot places and solid in colder environments. Keep this in mind when
formulating with coconut oil – that if your customer lives in a hot country, a solid product
formulated with coconut oil might become liquid. The unrefined version of this oil has
a strong coconut odour that might be desirable or not in your formulations. The refined
version is unscented.

Because coconut oil is rich in saturated fatty acids, it has a high oxidation resistance.
It contains high amounts of lauric acid, which presents antimicrobial activity as a free
fatty acid.

Also, this oil has moisturising effects, helping improve the skin barrier function. It is one of
the few oils able to penetrate the hair strand, as lauric acid has a high affinity for keratin. It
prevents the loss of hair proteins in both undamaged and damaged hair of different types
(straight, curly, wavy and permed hair). It helps make the hair more resistant to mechanical
damage. For these reasons, virgin coconut oil is beneficial for haircare, especially in
conditioners.

Although it doesn't always work in facial products, as some people report some sensitivity,
feel free to experiment with it in body skincare and haircare formulations.

Fractionated coconut oil, also known as medium-chain triglycerides, contains only part of
the coconut oil fatty acids. Even though it doesn't possess the same properties as coconut
oil, it is liquid and fluid, being used as a silicone replacement in some formulations.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Lip care, haircare, anhydrous creams, balms, masks, butters, scrubs, and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Not everyone likes its aroma. It can be liquid or solid, depending on the temperature.

name: Evening primrose oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Evening primrose has a long history in skincare. Native Americans used it to treat various
skin issues and also ate its roots. The oil is extracted from the seeds using a cold-pressing
method.

This oil is rich in unsaturated fatty acids, mainly gamma-linoleic acid, which makes it very
unstable to oxidation. To avoid rancidification, keep this oil away from light, heat, and
oxygen if possible.

Its unsaponifiable portion comprises about 1.5 – 2% of the oil. It contains triterpenes,
tocopherols, and phytosterols that have been studied for their anti-inflammatory,
antibacterial and antifungal activities.

This oil helps improve the skin barrier function and reduce transepidermal water loss
(TEWL), providing anti-inflammatory and repairing properties. It is often used for people
with dry, acne-prone, and irritated skin. In vivo studies suggest this oil may aid in skin repair.

This oil can be used in anti-ageing products, nourishing salves and balms.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
It can be added to the cool-down phase of emulsions. Use it in lip care, haircare, anhydrous
creams, balms, masks, butters, scrubs, and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Heat sensitive. Only add it to products under 40 °C (104 °F).

name: Flaxseed oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Flaxseed, also known as linseed, is one of the oldest oilseed crops grown and has various
usages besides cosmetics. It is useful in food, painting, varnish, and printing ink.

It tops all other sources of alpha-linolenic acid in the plant world. This oil has a high
concentration of this essential fatty acid, which presents anti-inflammatory properties and
is beneficial to the care of damaged and dry skin.

Even though this oil contains some vitamin E, it is still easily oxidised, rapidly becoming
rancid. Thus, additional antioxidants need to be added to protect this oil.

Flaxseed is known as a 'dry oil' because it quickly penetrates the top layers of the skin,
providing moisturising and soothing effects.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Anhydrous creams, balms, masks, butters, scrubs, and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Heat sensitive. Only add it to products under 40 °C (104 °F).

name: Fractionated coconut oil/ medium chain triglycerides (mct)
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Fractionated coconut oil is similar to medium-chain triglyceride (MCT), also known as
Caprylic/Capric Triglyceride (CCT), although they are not necessarily the same. These terms
are often used interchangeably, but the origin and processing of each material can differ.

Fractionated coconut oil is made by removing the long-chain fatty acids from coconut oil,
leaving only the medium-chain fatty acids (mainly caprylic and capric acids) in the form of
triglycerides. Because this fraction is composed of medium-chain triglycerides, the names
are often used as if they refer to the same material.

MCT, on the other hand, is a triglyceride containing medium-chain fatty acids, primarily
caprylic and capric acids. It can be produced by separating a fraction of coconut, palm,
or other oils, as described above. However, it can also be produced by hydrolysing these
oils to break them down into isolated fatty acids and glycerine, which are then separated.
The selected medium-chain fatty acids are then re-esterified with glycerine to form the
triglycerides.

Both fractionated coconut oil and MCT are fast-absorbing, lightweight emollients that
leave a soft and non-greasy feel on the skin, often serving as silicone alternatives. One of
their main advantages is their resistance to oxidation and the fact that they do not solidify
in cold weather, making it easier to create stable and uniform formulations. Additionally,
they lack the characteristic odour associated with coconut oil, making them neutral and
more versatile.

Fractionated coconut oil and MCT enhance the spreadability of creams and lotions,
solubilise lipophilic ingredients, and form a semi-occlusive film on the skin, helping to
reduce water loss and leaving a pleasant after-feel. They are common ingredients in
creams, serums, lotions, balms, lipsticks, and more, and are suitable for all skin types.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
AFractionated coconut oil and MCT can be added to emulsions, makeup, oil-based
formulations, and haircare formulations.

Both of these oils can substitute coconut oil since they do not solidify in cold weather and
have a smoother texture. Also, they do not have a significant odour and can be added to
formulations where the coconut scent is not desired. They can even be used as carriers
for oil-soluble fragrances.

They can be cold- or hot-processed since they are very heat-stable.

Fractionated coconut oil and MCT are light and non-greasy oils and great emollients.
They help to soften the skin and are suitable for all skin types, including oily skin, due
to their light texture.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Formulations containing fractionated coconut oil or MCT should not be packed in
containers with polystyrene in their composition since they can make the plastic brittle
upon contact.

name: Grapeseed oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Grapeseed oil comes from the seeds of the Vitis vinifera fruits. It is a by-product of the
leftovers of the wine-making process in many areas of the world.

Some manufacturers use solvents to extract this oil, often heating it in the process.
Frequently the refined oil is sold, and it is thinner and presents less colour and scent than
the unrefined version. The refined oil also contains fewer therapeutic properties, as it is
deprived of some of its active compounds.

This oil is rich in antioxidants in its unsaponifiable fraction. Some examples are vitamin E,
resveratrol, and phenolic compounds such as proanthocyanidins. Besides its antioxidant
action, an in vivo study suggested that this oil has a significant skin repair action. .

Grapeseed is very moisturising and is often used as a massage carrier oil.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Anhydrous products, balms, masks, butters, scrubs, and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Heat sensitive. Only add it to products under 40 °C (104 °F).

name: Hemp seed oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Hemp seed oil is cold-pressed from the seeds of Cannabis sativa or indica, one of the oldest
plants used by humans in history. It comes originally from Asia, but was cultivated in Europe
as well.

It should not be confused with CBD oil, which is an extract made from the plant's leaves and
flowers. Hemp oil is a dark green liquid at room temperature.

Tocopherols are widely known antioxidant compounds present in hemp seed oil, with the
content ranging from 80 to 150 mg/100 g oil. It also contains other minor components
such as polyphenols (mainly flavonoids), carotenoids, phytosterols, vitamins, and dietary
minerals. Although antioxidants are present in hemp seed oil, it is not very stable and is
prone to oxidation due to its high content of chlorophyll, which can act as a pro-oxidative
compound. Its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory compounds make it a great addition to
any skincare product.

Also, hemp seed oil's gamma-linolenic acid content makes it a great addition to products
for problem skin. It is considered beneficial for the care of dry and mature skin and soothing
irritated, itchy and inflamed skin.

As it is a dry oil, you can blend it with other carrier oils, such as apricot oil. You can combine
it with rosehip or kiwi oils to help balance sebum production and add it to serums and oils,
or use it in haircare with coconut oil.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Anhydrous creams, balms, masks, butters, scrubs and emulsions, haircare products. It is an
excellent oil for soap making as well.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It is prone to oxidation, so it is recommended to avoid heating the oil. Also, it has a strong
colour that can be imparted to your formulations.

name: Jojoba oil
substitution: No specific substitute COMPOSITION:  Wax esters – 40 and 42 carbon chain length esters.  Less than 1 % triglyceride content.  Vitamin E.
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Jojoba oil is in fact a wax that is liquid at room temperature. It is slightly viscous, has a
weak nutty odour and solidifies in temperatures below 10ºC.

This oil does not go rancid easily, exhibiting extraordinary thermal and oxidative stabilities.
Its tocopherol content helps in its long shelf-life.

The composition of jojoba oil is very similar to that of sebum, which is why this ingredient is
a fantastic moisturiser for the skin. It also contains anti-inflammatory compounds that can
help with various skin conditions and presents antimicrobial and antifungal activities.

Jojoba oil helps repair the skin lipid barrier, reducing transepidermal water loss and
controlling sebum production. It works for all skin and hair types, as it doesn't leave a
greasy feel but is especially useful for dry and acne-prone skin.

Also, jojoba oil helps gently unclog pores and remove grime from the skin and scalp. Thus, it
is an excellent addition to cleansing products.

It is a great choice for massage oils and products designed to protect the skin from the
elements.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in anhydrous products such as balms, masks, butters, and scrubs. You can also use it
in emulsions and haircare products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects known. No formulation restriction known.

name: Macadamia oil
inci: Macadamia Integrifolia Seed Oil or Macadamia Ternifolia Seed Oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Macadamia oil is obtained from the nuts of the macadamia tree. The nut itself is a rich
source of nutrients, including many different vitamins and minerals. This oil is resistant to
rancidity.

It is a rich carrier oil that possesses moisturising properties. It penetrates the top layers of
the skin rapidly and makes a pleasant massage oil.

Macadamia oil possesses high levels of palmitoleic acid, unlike any other known plant
oil. This fatty acid is also present in human sebum, decreasing with age, which is why
macadamia oil can be beneficial in anti-ageing formulations.

In vitro studies showed that isolated palmitoleic acid exhibits potential antimicrobial
activity. Also, it was able to decrease the synthesis of melanin by inhibiting the expression
of enzymes that produce melanin (tyrosinase and tyrosinase-related protein-1). These
results suggest that acne-prone and hyperpigmented skin could benefit from the use of
macadamia oil.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in anhydrous products such as balms, masks, butters, and scrubs. You can also use it
in emulsions and haircare products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects known. No formulation restriction known.

name: Marula oil
colour: Golden yellow with a hint of rose
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Belonging to the same botanical family as mango, marula oil is a botanical treasure from
Africa, where it is called “miracle oil”. It is used extensively in the western and southern
parts of the continent. This oil has various uses, including cooking and skincare, along with
burns and wounds treatment in traditional medicine.

Marula oil contains a large amount of monounsaturated fatty acids and natural
antioxidants. It can be classified as a high-oleic acid oil with relatively low tocopherol
content. It has good oxidative stability.

Along with its fatty acid composition, this oil contains various phytosterols. These are plant
compounds that promote barrier repair and help reduce transepidermal water loss, while
also presenting anti-inflammatory action.

Marula oil softens and soothes the complexion. It absorbs well into the skin and provides a
silky feel when used for massage and body conditioning.

Marula is a gentle oil that helps soothe sensitive skin and reduce redness and inflammation.
It is not only beneficial to the skin, but also the hair. It helps balance the scalp’s natural oil
without leaving a greasy residue.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in anhydrous products such as balms, masks, butters, and scrubs. You can also use it
in emulsions and haircare products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects known. No formulation restriction known.

name: Meadowfoam oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Meadowfoam oil is cold-pressed from the seeds of the meadowfoam flower. This plant
has this name because its blooming flowers resemble the ocean's white foam. In order to
prevent the hunting of whales for their oil, meadowfoam was used as an alternative.

This oil is one of the most resistant against oxidation due to its high amounts of vitamin E
and long-chain fatty acids. It remains very stable when exposed to oxygen and heat, even
helping extend the shelf-life of products in which it is included.

Despite being thick, meadowfoam oil has a non-greasy feeling and glides easily on the skin.
It has great moisturising properties and penetrates quickly into the top layers of the skin.
It is an excellent emollient that helps repair the lipid barrier, protecting the skin
and hair.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in anhydrous products such as balms, masks, butters, and scrubs. You can also use it
in emulsions and haircare products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects known. No formulation restriction known.

name: Moringa oil
scent: Weak odour reminiscent of fresh leaves
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Moringa oil is one of the ancient oils, along with flaxseed, castor, and olive. The traditional
cosmetic use of moringa oil has been known for thousands of years. The tree, as a whole, is
highly nutritious and all parts are used traditionally including the leaves, flowers, and roots,
along with the oil pressed from the seeds.

The main characteristic of moringa oil is its fatty acid composition, which has unusual
amounts of behenic acid. This very long, 22 carbon-chain saturated fatty acid gives the oil
its velvety skin feel and helps to protect skin and hair against oxidation and environmental
damage. Moringa oil was the first discovered source of behenic fatty acid and as a result,
moringa oil is also called behenic oil, or ben oil for short. Its phytosterols content is also
quite remarkable, with beta-sitosterol as the dominant component (47% of phytosterols).

Very stable against oxidation, this oil has good slip characteristics due to its long-chain
fatty acids. These properties make moringa oil an interesting choice for colour cosmetics.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in lipsticks, balms, bath melts, shampoos, hair conditioners, and hair balms.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects known. No formulation restriction known.

name: Neem oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Neem oil is cold-pressed from the seeds of the evergreen neem tree, which grows on
the Indian subcontinent. It varies in colour and has a strong fragrance that resembles
something between a peanut and garlic. The garlic-like scent is due to sulphur compounds.
It is a semi-solid oil due to its high content of palmitic and stearic acids.

Neem is well-known for its home use in treating head lice, which says something about its
insecticide properties. It is also strongly anti-inflammatory and has a long history of use in
traditional herbal medicine.

Neem oil is often recommended to soothe dry, inflamed, and irritated skin. Laboratory
in vivo studies have demonstrated neem oil provides anti-inflammatory, skin repair, and
antimicrobial effects. These findings suggest that neem oil is a good choice for the care of
acne-prone skin.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in lipsticks, balms, bath melts, shampoos, hair conditioners, and hair balms.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Neem oil has a strong scent that is frequently described as unpleasant. It can leave a strong
colouration in a product. Some very rare cases of contact dermatitis have been reported.

name: Olive oil
colour: Greenish yellow to strong green colour
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Everyone knows olive oil for its culinary uses, but it also plays a significant role in the history
of cosmetics. Olive oil has a long history of being used as a home remedy for skincare.
The Egyptians have used it alongside beeswax as a cleanser, moisturiser, and antibacterial
agent since the times of the Pharaohs. Cleopatra was said to use olive oil as
a skin treatment.

Olive oil is obtained from the flesh of the olive fruit, not the kernel. The black olive can
contain as much as 50% oil. These are mechanically cold-pressed when ripe and can be
further filtered. The best one we recommend in natural cosmetics is the cold-pressed,
extra virgin oil. Extra virgin olive oil has the added advantage of containing remarkable
antioxidants, making it a natural anti-ageing ingredient. These natural antioxidants are often
destroyed during the processing or refining of lower quality oils. That is the reason why it is
better to buy the best cold-pressed olive oil you can find.

It is a rich oil, which makes it useful in nourishing products. Olive oil is used as an emollient
ingredient and has a high oleic acid content. It also contains large amounts of vitamin E,
phytosterols and squalene.

Free oleic acid is a well-documented skin penetration enhancer. This might be related to the
findings of some reports that suggest that olive oil could compromise the stratum corneum
barrier and increase transepidermal water loss. So, it is better to use it combined with
other vegetable oils instead of as a standalone ingredient, especially in paediatric skincare
or products for people with dry skin conditions. However, we recommend olive squalane,
which is another emollient derived from olives.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in anhydrous products such as balms, masks, butters, and scrubs. You can also use it
in emulsions and haircare products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects known. No formulation restriction known.

name: Passionfruit seed oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Passionfruit seed oil is also known as maracuja oil, and it is cold-pressed from the fruit's
seeds. It has a long history of use by the Aztecs.

This oil is one of the best sources of linoleic acid and contains about 1% of unsaponifiables:
mainly carotenoids, vitamin E and flavonoids. It has a high vitamin E content (around 499.30
mg/kg).

A light emollient, it is said to have anti-inflammatory properties as well as helping to relieve
itching. Use it for dry, itchy and irritated skin and after-sun products. Quickly absorbed
into the skin, passion fruit oil is also helpful for the care of acne-prone skin. Its fatty acid
composition contributes to its ability in creating a protective layer on the skin while being
easily absorbed without leaving a greasy skin feel.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in anhydrous products such as balms, masks, butters, and scrubs. You can also use it
in emulsions and haircare products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects known. No formulation restriction known.

name: Pomegranate seed oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Pomegranate seed oil is obtained from the seeds of the pomegranate fruit. Pomegranate
oil is rich in anti-ageing compounds and is used in small percentages to give your skincare
product a high-performance boost.

It is composed predominantly of unsaturated fatty acids with punicic acid, a very rare
omega-5 fatty acid, representing about 80% of its total fatty acid composition. Punicic
acid is an unsaturated fatty acid with twisted carbon chains that make pomegranate oil
feel thick and rich. According to the literature, it may have beneficial anti-inflammatory
effects. However, the fatty acid profile of this oil can vary depending on cultivation factors.
Pomegranate oil also contains polyphenols with a remarkable antioxidant activity.

This oil is said to rejuvenate your skin by improving its elasticity and collagen production.
It helps speed up the shedding of dead skin cells and stimulates keratinocytes proliferation
while helping repair the skin lipid barrier. The antioxidants in pomegranate oil help protect
against stress from environmental exposure.

Pomegranate is a rich and nourishing oil that is great for any skincare product. It is an
excellent choice for products directed to mature and dry skin. It also helps in the care of
sensitive skin and works well in after-sun skincare products. Even when used in small
amounts, it can make a difference.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in anhydrous products such as balms, masks, butters, and scrubs. You can also use it
in emulsions and haircare products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects known. It is a sensitive oil, so you should only use it once your formula
is under 40 °C (104 °F). If you are making emulsions, it should be added during the cool down phase.
It has a strong aroma.

name: Pracaxi oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Pracaxi oil is obtained from the seeds of the pracaxi tree. It is also called the oil bean tree.
This oil has the highest known concentration of behenic acid and has a heavy and thick
skin feel. It may have a mild or strong nutty aroma. It is solid at room temperature in the
temperate zone yet melts on contact with the skin.

Indigenous people from the Amazonian region use pracaxi oil as an insect repellent and in
the care of stretch marks. It also helps brighten the skin, minimise scarring, and contains
compounds with anti-haemorrhagic properties.

Pracaxi oil has excellent moisturising properties. It is widely used in skincare and makeup
products. It brings many benefits to hair products and is used especially in conditioners and
hair masks.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in anhydrous products such as balms, masks, butters, and scrubs. You can also use it
in emulsions and haircare products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects known. No formulation restriction known.

name: Rice bran oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Rice bran oil is not derived from seeds like most other oils, but from the bran of the rice
grain. For this reason, its composition is unusual when compared to other plant oils – it has
a high wax content, for example.

The refining process of rice bran oil is tricky, meaning that it isn’t easy to get hold of it for
commercial use. But if you can, it’s a great oil to use.

It has high levels of gamma-oryzanol, which is a mixture of esters of ferulic acid and
triterpene alcohols or sterols, only found in rice bran oil. Its concentration goes up to 2%
in crude oil. This compound is a powerful antioxidant, also presenting anti-inflammatory
properties. It may also be useful to reduce wrinkles and hyperpigmentation.

Because it is rich in antioxidants and essential fatty acids, rice bran oil is an excellent
moisturiser. It is great for dry, mature, and sensitive skin. It can also be used in hair
products, as it gives hair shine without weighing it down. Also, this oil is mild enough to be
used in baby skincare products.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in anhydrous products such as balms, masks, butters, and scrubs. You can also use it
in emulsions and haircare products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
A study suggested that gamma-oryzanol and alpha-tocopherol may act as antagonists
in O/W emulsions. So, you might need to observe the stability of your products if you use
these two ingredients together or if you pair rice bran oil with tocopherol rich oils.

name: Rosehip oil
inci: Rosa Rubiginosa Seed Oil or Rosa Moschata Seed Oil or Rosa Canina Fruit Oil.
substitution: Raspberry oil, but it does not contain any vitamin A derivative
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Rosehip oil is extracted from the seeds of Rosa rubiginosa, Rosa moschata, or the fruit of
Rosa canina. Although rosehips grow in many parts of the world, Chile is one of its main
producers. This oil has quick absorption and provides a silky skin feel.

Rosehip oil has high amounts of linoleic and alpha-linolenic acids, two essential fatty acids.
They help repair the skin lipid barrier and provide anti-inflammatory properties.

Rosehip oil also contains carotenoids (lycopene, beta-carotene, and rubixanthin),
which contribute to its reddish colour. Another interesting compound found in this
oil is trans-retinoic acid (tretinoin), a derivative of vitamin A (retinol). It helps reduce
hyperpigmentation, improve acne-prone skin, and provide rejuvenating properties. Keep in
mind that these compounds are not present in the refined version of this oil.

There are some doubts if this oil is really suitable for acne-prone skin. A study about free
linoleic acid suggests it can help reduce microcomedones in patients with mild acne.
However, it is unsure if these results could be expanded to oils containing high amounts of
linolenic acid, which is the case of rosehip oil.

Rosehip oil helps smooth and prevent wrinkles, slowing down the signs of ageing. It
also helps prevent scars and improve their appearance. That is one of the reasons
why it is popularly valued as a good choice for acne-prone skin, especially those with
hyperpigmentation and scars. Also, this oil provides antibacterial and antifungal properties.

Although many say that rosehip oil is a great source of vitamin C, this information
is incorrect. Oils and butters do not contain water-soluble vitamins like vitamin C in
significant amounts.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in anhydrous products such as balms, masks, butters, and scrubs. You can also use it
in emulsions and haircare products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It is a sensitive oil, so you should only use it once your formula is under 40 °C (104 °F). If you are
making emulsions, it should be added during the cool down phase.

name: Safflower oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Safflower oil comes from the seeds of the Carthamus tinctorius plant. The flowers look like
a thistle but with red or orange flowers, which is why it is also known as ‘thistle oil’.

Safflower oil is high in essential fatty acids and is beneficial for any skin type, given its
mildness. It is a light and quickly absorbed oil, also used as a colouring agent in cosmetics,
and helps dry and sensitive skin.

One of the richest sources of linoleic acid, safflower oil presents anti-inflammatory
properties and helps repair the skin lipid barrier.

Safflower oil is a good choice for oily and acne-prone skin. For the care of dry skin, it can be
combined with vegetable butters.

Safflower oil thickens and becomes rancid when exposed to air, so make sure you keep this
oil away from exposure to oxygen as much as possible.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in anhydrous products such as balms, masks, butters, and scrubs. You can also use it
in emulsions and haircare products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It is a sensitive oil, so you should only use it once your formula is under 40 °C (104 °F). If you are
making emulsions, it should be added during the cool down phase.

name: Sesame oil
function: Emollient, hair conditioning, fragrance, skin conditioning
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Sesame oil is well-known for its culinary uses, especially in Asia. Besides this, it also
presents many cosmetic benefits. It has similar properties to olive oil and contains
antioxidants that make it very stable. It has a high content of vitamins E and K.

Sesame oil is used to treat dry, sensitive, and itchy skin conditions. It works as a softener
and moisturiser and is great in massage oils or as a carrier for botanical macerations.

In vitro studies have demonstrated the antioxidant activity of some of its compounds,
sesamolin and sesamin. Sesame oil may therefore be beneficial in the care of mature and
stressed skin.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in anhydrous products such as balms, masks, butters, and scrubs. You can also use it
in emulsions and haircare products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects known. No formulation restriction known.

name: Soybean oil
inci: Glycine Soja Oil or Glycine Max Oil
substitution: Close to corn oil and quinoa oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Soybean oil is a vegetable oil extracted from the seeds of Glycine soja or Glycine max.
Soybeans don’t contain much oil (about 20%), so cold pressing doesn’t yield large quantities
of oil. Most soybean oil is produced by solvent extraction. This oil is a good source of
vitamin E.

Soybean oil is used in many foods and cosmetic products. Due to its low price, it is often
found in soaps, hair, and skincare products. Soy is usually a genetically modified plant. So,
if you wish to use non-GMO ingredients in your skincare, you may have to ask your suppliers
about the oil’s origin. High-quality soybean oil is hard to find, but it proves to be very useful
for dry, sensitive, irritated, and allergy-prone skin.

Some of the most interesting properties of soybean oil come from its unsaponifiable matter.
It contains up to 3% phospholipids, such as lecithin. Lecithin significantly contributes to the
moisturising effects and weak emulsifying properties of soybean oil. An in vitro and in vivo
laboratory study has shown that soybean isoflavones can reduce photodamaging effects in
keratinocytes.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in anhydrous products such as balms, masks, butters, and scrubs. You can also use it
in emulsions and haircare products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Soybean oil can also be solvent extracted, so search for cold-pressed soybean oil if you
want the pure, unadulterated oil. No adverse effects known. No formulation restriction
known.

name: Sunflower oil
heatStability: Poor, but may depend on the type of sunflower oil
oxidationStability: Unstable, but may depend on the type of sunflower oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Organic sunflower oil is cold-pressed using the seeds from sunflower heads, whilst
commercially produced sunflower oil is extracted with solvents.

It is a light, moisturising oil, effective as the base oil for light creams. It is also great for
massage oils or used as a carrier oil in aromatherapy. As an emollient, it can be used in
cleansing cosmetic products for the skin and hair.

There are different types of sunflower seed oils based on their fatty acid profile: high
linoleic, mid-oleic, high oleic and high stearic/high oleic. The higher the monounsaturated
and saturated fatty acids content in the oil, the more stable to heat and oxidation it is.
Linoleic acid, the predominant fatty acid in high linoleic sunflower seed oil, helps repair the
skin lipid barrier.

It is high in vitamins D and E, as well as lecithin. Sunflower is becoming increasingly popular
as a substitute for soybean, representing an alternative source for the production of lecithin
due to the unacceptability of genetically modified soybean in natural cosmetics.

Because it is widely available at an affordable price, it can be perceived as a low-quality oil.
However, sunflower oil can be beneficial for the care of dry, irritated and inflamed skin.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in anhydrous products such as balms, masks, butters, and scrubs. You can also use it
in emulsions and haircare products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects known. No formulation restriction known.

name: Sweet almond oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Sweet almond oil is a popular and versatile ingredient that can be used in massage oils and
as a carrier oil in aromatherapy and other cosmetic products such as emulsions. It is able to
form a protective layer over the skin, helping to retain moisture and prevent transepidermal
water loss.

This oil is rich in beta-sitosterol, squalene, and alpha-tocopherol (vitamin E). It is one of the
best sources of vitamin E, which protects healthy cells from damage by free radicals. This
oil benefits all skin types, as it leaves the skin feeling soft, nourished, and revitalised.

Freshly extracted almond oil has a low peroxide value combined with high tocopherol
content, presenting moderate stability against oxidation.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in anhydrous products such as balms, masks, butters, and scrubs. You can also use
it in emulsions and haircare products. It is great for massage oils, as well as natural
perfume bases.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
People with nut allergies should be cautious when using sweet almond oil.

Sweet almond oil can also be solvent extracted, so search for cold-pressed sweet almond
oil if you want the pure, unadulterated oil.

name: Tamanu seed oil
function: Antimicrobial, antioxidant, hair conditioning, oral care, skin conditioning
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Tamanu oil comes from the Calophyllum inophyllum seeds. It is a thick, green, and slightly
viscous oil. The oil is referred to as “green gold” for its colour and reputed repairing
properties.

Its main feature is its unique composition of unsaponifiable matter, which includes
terpenoids (canophyllol and canophyllic acid) and phenols (calophyllic acid, calophylloids
and inophylloids).

Although this oil is slowly becoming more popular in cosmetics in recent years, it has been
the subject of scientific literature for many years. Based on traditional folklore and scientific
literature, tamanu oil helps in the care of damaged, inflamed, and acne-prone skin.

With an unusual composition, tamanu oil has been demonstrated to repair the skin and
diminish scarring. On healthy skin, tamanu oil will help maintain a healthy glow.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in anhydrous products such as balms, masks, butters, and scrubs. You can also use
it in emulsions and haircare products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Although there are no safety/legal limits, this oil is not commonly used as a standalone oil
but is usually added at 1-20% and combined with other oils.

In winter, the oil might solidify. Gently heat between 25 – 35 °C (77 – 95 °F) and shake the container
before using the oil.

Scientific literature describes a rare case of contact dermatitis due to the topical use of
Calophyllum oil. So, it is best to use it in low concentrations in cosmetic products.

This oil might impart a dark colour to the formulation.

name: Beeswax
function: Skin conditioning, emollient, emulsifying, emulsion stabilising, viscosity controlling, film forming, binding, perfuming
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Beeswax is a natural wax produced by honey bees. The worker bees secrete it to build the
honeycomb walls, where they store their honey to protect it. It makes the comb resistant
to weather conditions and keeps the inside free from contaminants.

Beeswax has been used for centuries to make candles. They are said to be the healthiest
candles, as they do not emit toxic by-products. Beeswax has also been used in art as an
ingredient in paints. Nowadays, it is still one of the best skin softening ingredients.

Beeswax is a natural thickener. You could add it to products where the consistency needs
to be improved or where you need a higher Melting point, for example, in lip balms.

Beeswax creates an occlusive layer on the skin, creating a protective barrier and trapping
in moisture, decreasing the transepidermal water loss. Some sources recommend this
wax as an emulsifier, but this is not true: it only helps to stabilise the emulsion, especially
W/O emulsions.

Beeswax demonstrates some antioxidant activity thanks to its polyphenols' content, along
with some anti-inflammatory properties.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in facial, body, and lip balms, body butters, or in any product that requires a firmer
structure. It can also be used in emulsions in a small amount.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Beeswax is not suitable for vegan formulations. It is not recommended to heat it above
85 °C (185 °F), which can cause discolouration. It can have a heavy skin feel when used in
facial products.

name: Berry wax
inci: Rhus Verniciflua Peel Cera or Rhus Verniciflua Peel Wax
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Berry wax is a soft wax with a light colour. It is extracted from the berries of Rhus
verniciflua. This wax should not be confused with sumac wax (also called Japan wax),
extracted from Rhus succedanea, a plant from the same genus. Always refer to the INCI
name instead of the common names to avoid confusion. The plant is called varnish tree or
lacquer tree because the stem exudate is used in the production of Japanese lacquer.

Berry wax has a high ester content and consists mainly of esters of palmitic acid, stearic
acid and a unique C21 fatty acid: heneicosylic acid. Because of its softness and low
Melting point, it is not suitable for stick formulations as a standalone wax. Its main
applications are in cosmetic pencil production or emulsion stabilisation, as well as
in balms.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Berry wax is used to stabilise emulsions and oleogels. It also helps avoid breakage and
improve the skin feel of cosmetic pencil formulations, such as eyebrow or eyeliner pencils.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It is a vegan alternative to beeswax, but it has a lower Melting point. Consider it when
formulating and combine it with high Melting point waxes, if necessary, especially in
stick formulations.

name: Candelilla wax
inci: Euphorbia Cerifera Cera or Euphorbia Cerifera Wax
function: Emollient, skin conditioning, emulsion stabilising, viscosity controlling, film forming, perfuming
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Candelilla wax is derived from the leaves of the small candelilla shrub, native to northern
Mexico and the southwestern United States. The plant is boiled to separate the wax
and the plant material. The wax floats to the top of the water and is skimmed off and
processed.

It is a natural thickener, just like beeswax. You can add it to products where the
consistency needs to be improved or in which you need more hardness, as in lip balms,
for example. Since it has a higher Melting point than beeswax, you can use it in lower
amounts in your formulations.

Candelilla is considered a hard, brittle wax, which provides excellent oil binding properties.
It gives a glossy look to lip products such as lip balms and lipsticks and creates an
occlusive layer on the skin.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
It is used to help stabilise stick formulations, thicken anhydrous formulations and adjust
the viscosity of water-in-oil emulsions.

Because of its high Melting point, it is also used in mascaras and lipsticks, to which it gives
shine.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It is a vegan alternative to beeswax, but as it has a different hardness and texture,
formulations might need adjustment.

name: Carnauba wax
inci: Copernicia Cerifera Wax or Copernicia Cerifera Cera
function: Film forming, skin conditioning, emollient, depilatory
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Carnauba wax is extracted from the leaves of the carnauba palm tree (Copernicia cerifera),
native to Brazil. The wax is produced as a leaf exudate that helps prevent the leaves from
dehydration.

It is available from very dark intensive yellow to light beige colour and is available as
flakes, pellets, or powder. Carnauba has the highest Melting point among natural waxes.

Carnauba wax imparts hardness and reduces stickiness in cosmetic formulations.
It is often added to mascara formulations as a volumising agent.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Lip balms, balm deodorants, any stick formulations. It can also be used in body butters.

Just like candelilla, carnauba wax has a high Melting point. As a result, it is often used
in mascaras and lipsticks.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It is a vegan alternative to beeswax, but as it has a different hardness and texture,
formulations might need adjustment. It cannot be used on its own in stick formulations
and has to be combined with another wax such as beeswax or candelilla wax.

name: Myrica fruit wax
function: Emollient, film forming, skin conditioning and viscosity controlling
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Myrica wax is obtained from the berry fruit peels of the Myrica cerifera tree, native to
North and Central America and the Caribbean. This wax contains predominantly saturated
long-chain fatty acids, which makes it unique since it can have similar properties to oils,
but it is solid. Considering it has no double bonds and has a low iodine value (<2), myrica
wax is very stable against oxidation. It has a low Melting point and, as it is composed
by saturated fatty acids, it is slightly harder than common vegetable butters, presenting
excellent spreadability.

This wax can help stabilise stick formulations, reduce the stickiness of O/W emulsions
and oleogels, and works for hairstyling products. It can be used in hair conditioners
in combination with fatty alcohols. Myrica fruit wax imparts a nice skin feel to balms,
butters, and hairstyling products.

It doesn’t contribute much to hardness and mainly adds texture, body (without
greasiness), and emulsion stabilisation to cosmetic products.

Since it has a low Melting point, it solidifies very slowly. This leads to a pleasant and
smooth texture of the products made with myrica wax.

It suits stick products such as lip or face balms packed in tubes, but is not hard enough to
be used as the standalone wax for lipsticks.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Lip balms, balm deodorants, any stick formulations. It can also be used in body butters.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It is a vegan alternative to beeswax, but as it has a different hardness and texture,
formulations might need adjustment. It cannot be used on its own in stick formulations
and has to be combined with another wax such as beeswax or candelilla wax.

name: Rice bran wax
inci: Oryza Sativa Cera or Oryza Sativa Bran Cera or Oryza Sativa Bran Wax
function: Skin conditioning, skin protecting, hair conditioning, smoothing, and viscosity controlling
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Rice bran wax is obtained by dewaxing virgin rice bran oil. It is a pale yellow hard wax
available in pellets, beads, or powder. It is composed mainly of esters of C16-C24 fatty
acids with C26-C32 alcohols.

This wax has a nice, non-sticky skin feel in emulsions, balms, and butters. One of its
specific applications is in lipsticks to inhibit syneresis (the expulsion or “sweating” of
liquid from the crystalline structure). It can also be used in hairstyling products.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
It is used in oil-in-water emulsions, balms, butters, lipstick, and hairstyling products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It is a vegan alternative to beeswax, but as it has a different hardness and texture,
formulations might need adjustment.

name: Sunflower wax
inci: Helianthus Annuus Seed Cera or Helianthus Annuus Seed Wax
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Sunflower wax is obtained by dewaxing sunflower oil. It has a pale yellow colour and is
available as beads, chunks, or pellets.

Sunflower wax has a high oil binding capacity. It provides a non-sticky skin feel, imparts
gloss to formulations and stabilises water-in-oil emulsions.

This wax contains approximately 30% hydrocarbons and 70% fatty esters. Behenyl
acetate, lignoceryl acetate and methyl lignocerate are the main wax esters.

In O/W emulsions, this wax is not able to form a stable network. Therefore, it should be
used only in W/O emulsions or anhydrous products.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Water-in-oil emulsions, oil-based products, as well as haircare and decorative products
(lipstick) where gloss is desired.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It is a vegan alternative to beeswax, but as it has a different hardness and texture,
formulations might need adjustment.

name: Lavender hydrosol
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Lavandula angustifolia hydrosol exerts cooling, hydrating, toning actions with antibacterial
properties.

The main components of the volatile fraction of lavender hydrosols are linalool,
alpha-terpineol, borneol and geraniol.

Lavender hydrosol works well in soothing products such as after-sun mists or those
designed for night use. Gentle and balancing, it suits all skin types.

Blend it with chamomile for calming mists, with geranium and rose hydrosols for mature
skin, or try it with rosemary hydrosol in shampoos or conditioners. It also works well with
peppermint in refreshing shower foams. It may also help with the itchiness of the skin
or scalp.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Try it in toners, mists, cleansers, shampoos, masques, and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
The scent of lavender hydrosol may be considered overwhelming to some formulators.

name: Lemon peel hydrosol
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Lemon peel hydrosol is a source of natural compounds such as geraniol and citral that
can inhibit the activity of the enzyme tyrosinase, which is involved in the production of
melanin. That means it could possibly help even the skin tone.

The hydrosol has a strong lemon aroma and can be incorporated into formulations
requiring a citrusy fragrance.

This is a very refreshing hydrosol that presents antibacterial properties and is also
astringent.

Blend it with any other hydrosol that can work with its uplifting lemony fragrance, such as
peppermint or a floral one like lavender or even neroli.

It can be a great addition to a product used in the morning, such as an uplifting shower gel
or a refreshing toner.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Try it in toners, mists, cleansers, shampoos, masques, and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
We recommend that you always check the SDS sheet before purchasing a hydrosol from a
new supplier.

name: Melissa hydrosol
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Melissa officinalis, also called lemon balm and balm mint, produces a hydrosol with
a beautiful lemony fragrance.

The most important components in lemon balm hydrosol are carvacrol, neral, and
geranial (citral).

Melissa hydrosol is astringent (skin tightening), working well in high-performance facial
mists. It suits oily skin with larger pores or can be used anytime the skin needs a
wake-up call.

With an uplifting and relaxing scent, this hydrosol blends well with lavender and other
floral hydrosols. It also works well with peppermint and rosemary.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Try it in toners, mists, cleansers, shampoos, masques, and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
We recommend that you always check the SDS sheet before purchasing a hydrosol from a
new supplier.

name: Orange blossom – neroli hydrosol
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Neroli was named after a small town near Rome called Nerola. Its princess made it
fashionable to use the bitter orange essence as a perfume. Since that time, the name
“Neroli” has been used to describe this fragrance.

This hydrosol is produced by steam distillation of the fresh flowers from Citrus aurantium
once the essential oil is removed by decantation.

The orange blossom water has been used for a long time in gastronomy, skincare
and perfumery.

It has been traditionally used in skincare for acne and oily skin due to its astringent
properties. Neroli hydrosol is a soothing and antimicrobial ingredient, even suitable for
