sensitive or delicate skin. It contains small amounts of linalool and alpha-terpineol.

It is a wonderfully subtle aromatic ingredient that can be used alone or blended with other
hydrosols. This hydrosol is refreshing and regenerating, working well with rose hydrosol
on mature skin. It blends well with peppermint in a refreshing shower foam or in facial
cleansers. Also, it works well when combined with Monoi de Tahiti oil in an emulsion.
It is also great in products without essential oils, where you would still wish to keep
a subtle scent.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Try it in toners, mists, cleansers, shampoos, masques, and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
We recommend that you always check the SDS sheet before purchasing a hydrosol from a
new supplier.

name: Peppermint hydrosol
function: Fragrance, perfuming, skin conditioning, deodorising, refreshing and tonic
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Peppermint (Mentha piperita) hydrosol exerts a cooling effect on the skin, caused by
two compounds present in small quantities: menthol and menthone. Menthol performs
cooling actions, helping to soothe and alleviate the sensations of warmth and the
tenseness of sun-irritated skin.

This hydrosol provides cooling effects in skin and haircare products.

It is antiseptic and very refreshing.

Use it in products created to be applied after exercising or in formulas designed to be part
of the morning skincare ritual.

It blends well with other floral waters, but be cautious as it can be strong and overpower
other hydrosols. Blend it with lavender, or pair it with rosemary in haircare products. It is
also works well with ylang-ylang and rose.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Try it in toners, mists, cleansers, shampoos, masques, and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
We recommend that you always check the SDS sheet before purchasing a hydrosol from a
new supplier.

name: Rose hydrosol
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Rose hydrosol is among the most widely produced and used floral waters worldwide.
Although rose water can be produced from different rose species, Rosa damascena is the
most popular for rose oil and water production.

Phenylethyl alcohol, geraniol, and citronellol are the main compounds of rose hydrosol.
In vitro studies suggest that rose hydrosol has antioxidant activity.

This hydrosol has a subtle floral aroma and is very gentle and rejuvenating. It suits mature
skin or any product designed to be soothing. Use it when you need a floral water for
irritated or acne-prone skin or products for damaged hair.

Rose hydrosol blends well with other floral waters. Blend it with lavender or pair it with
neroli. Use it with chamomile for sensitive skin products. Because rose essential oil/
absolute is very restricted in skincare, this can be an alternative way to incorporate rose
into natural skincare products.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Try it in toners, mists, cleansers, shampoos, masques, and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
We recommend that you always check the SDS sheet before purchasing a hydrosol from a
new supplier.

name: Witch hazel hydrosol
function: Astringent, hair conditioning, skin conditioning, soothing
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Witch hazel, or Hamamelis virginiana, is historically used for burns and injuries. With
astringent and anti-inflammatory effects, hamamelis preparations are classically applied
for disorders caused by dry skin conditions.

It is a good ingredient for acne-prone and problematic skin due to its astringent and
antibacterial properties. You can also use it in aftershave products, as it provides soothing
and anti-inflammatory actions.

It blends well with other floral waters. Blend it with lavender or with chamomile for
sensitive skin products. Try it with aloe powder or aloe gel.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Try it in toners, mists, cleansers, shampoos, masques, and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Hamamelis distillate is often sold with around 14% alcohol, so check this information with
your supplier. We recommend that you always check the SDS sheet before purchasing a
hydrosol from a new supplier.

name: Glycerine
function: Denaturant, skin conditioning, hair conditioning, skin protecting, humectant, solvent, perfuming
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Glycerine, or glycerol, is a natural constituent of triglycerides (glycerine + fatty acids).
The glycerol molecule is separated from the fatty acids during the saponification process
(soap-making). After this, it can be isolated from the soap and sold separately.

It works as a humectant for both the skin and the formulation, as it is a self-preserving
ingredient that attracts and holds moisture. Thus, it prevents water loss from the skin and
cosmetic products. That is the reason it is often found in items such as toothpaste, which
might otherwise dry out.

CHARACTERISTICS
• Temperature stable – you can heat it if necessary.
   • Soluble in water – add it to the water phase in emulsions or any water-based
     products, such as toners, micellar waters, shampoo, and gels.
   • Its moisture-binding properties help delay water evaporation from formulation,
     control viscosity, and impact body and feel of emulsion.
   • It gives products softness, flexibility, creaminess and improves shelf life.

COMPOSITION
Glycerine is highly hygroscopic, water-soluble, clear, colourless, viscous, odourless and
sweet-tasting, with low toxicity to human health and the environment.

Glycerine can have animal or vegetable origin, so check this information with your
supplier.

Also, it can have different grades, such as USP glycerine, CP glycerine, food-grade,
and others.

In skincare, it is used as a humectant, helping to keep the skin hydrated. Additionally, it
serves as a solvent for other substances, such as in glycerites, where it is used to extract
active compounds from botanicals.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in water-based products, glycerites, haircare and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
A high concentration of glycerine can create an undesirable sticky feeling on the skin.

name: Honey
function: Flavouring, emollient, humectant, moisturising, skin conditioning
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Honey is a bee-derived saccharic secretion. It is produced and stored by honey bees.

Honey is used in skincare for the same reason as glycerine. It is a humectant that attracts
and traps moisture on the skin. It also presents many beneficial properties for the skin as
it is rich in nutrients and antioxidants.

CHARACTERISTICS
• Hygroscopic (attracts and binds to water)
   • Cleansing properties
   • Antimicrobial and antioxidant properties
   • Soluble in water
   • Exerts emollient, humectant, soothing, and hair conditioning effects

Honey’s humectant properties come along with many other beneficial effects provided by
its biologically active compounds. And as if all of that isn’t enough, honey also possesses
antibacterial properties.

Manuka (Leptospermum scoparium) honey is often praised for its remarkable antibacterial
activity.

Honey nurtures the skin and contributes to regulating the mildly acidic pH of the upper
protective skin layer. It shows anti-irritant properties, making it a good ingredient for
sensitive skin. It can be used in a variety of cosmetic products.

COMPOSITION
• Supersaturated solution composed mainly of fructose and glucose.
     These carbohydrates are responsible for honey's hydrating properties.
   • It contains various nutrients, including amino acids, enzymes, organic acids,
     vitamins, and minerals like phosphorus, potassium, calcium, magnesium, sulphur,
     iron, copper, manganese, and zinc.
   • Also, it is a potent source of antioxidants, which can vary depending on the
     botanical origin of the honey. They can include chrysin, pinobanksin, vitamin C,
     catalase and pinocembrin.
   • Darker types of honey are richer in phenolic compounds like flavonoids and tannins
     and possess the strongest antioxidant activities.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in water-based products, emulsions, and haircare products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Even though allergy to honey is uncommon, it contains allergens such as pollen and bee
secretions that can function as sensitisers.

Honey can cause preservation issues in water-containing products, so try to use cosmetic-
grade honey or even freeze-dried honey powder. Remember, only challenge testing can
confirm if your preservation is adequate.

name: Hyaluronic acid and sodium hyaluronate hyaluronic acid
Sodium hyaluronate
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Hyaluronic acid is a polysaccharide component that is part of the glycosaminoglycans
group. It occurs naturally in the human body, with more than 50% of it found in the dermis,
where it plays a critical role in maintaining the structure and hydration of the skin.

A natural moisturiser and humectant, hyaluronic acid is well-known for its excellent water-
binding abilities. The ability to retain water helps improve skin appearance and bring
smoothness to rough skin.

Sodium hyaluronate, the sodium salt of hyaluronic acid, is very soluble and is the most
commonly used form.

It is now common to find different types of hyaluronic acids, but their primary difference lies
in their molecular weight. Hyaluronic acid with high molecular weight creates a light and
non-sticky film on the skin while retaining water in the stratum corneum without penetrating
the deeper layers. On the other end, hyaluronic acid with low molecular weight has no
film-forming or gel-creating abilities, but penetrates deeper into the epidermis. For this
reason, it is highly recommended to blend at least two different molecular weights in your
formulations to get the most out of the ingredient.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in water-based products like serums and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
While this ingredient’s strength is its ability to absorb moisture, it also requires a certain
procedure to add it to a formula for this very reason. If you blend hyaluronic acid directly
into the water phase, it will absorb the water quickly and swell while creating clumps that
are very hard to dissolve. In order to avoid that, the easiest way to dissolve it is to sprinkle
sodium hyaluronate into the water phase while stirring. Sprinkling it in the vortex created by
a magnetic stirrer is very effective, but a spatula is enough for small batches as well.

Hyaluronic acid was formerly produced from rooster's combs, but today it comes from
other natural sources as well. So, ask the supplier for information about the source of this
humectant, especially for vegan formulations.

For the effects of hyaluronic acid to last, the product needs to be applied regularly, as it is
broken down by the skin 24 to 48 hours after application (this does not apply to hyaluronic
acid injection).

name: Panthenol
function: Antistatic, hair conditioning, skin conditioning, humectant
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Panthenol, also known as pro-vitamin B5, is a precursor of pantothenic acid (vitamin B5).
Pantothenic acid is required to produce coenzyme A, an essential component of various
metabolic pathways in the human body. It helps stimulate the growth of skin cells and
increases the production of skin lipids, which improves the skin’s protective barrier.

The main function of panthenol in cosmetic formulas is to moisturise the skin and hair
and strengthen the hair shaft, but D-panthenol also shows anti-inflammatory, barrier-
repairing and soothing properties.

CHARACTERISTICS
• Water-soluble, should be added to the water phase of the formulation.
   • It is moisturising, anti-inflammatory, soothing, and helps promote skin repair.
   • Can be used to alleviate dry skin and as a soothing and moisturising agent in creams,
     lotions, and body washes.
   • Can also be used in shampoos and conditioners to improve shine and the hair’s
     elasticity and strength.
   • In nail care formulations, it helps make them less brittle.
   • If you are looking for an improved skin barrier and anti-inflammatory action,
     D-panthenol is a better choice. If you are aiming at hydrating the skin, both D or
     D,L-panthenol can be good options.

COMPOSITION
Panthenol can be found as either D-panthenol or as a mixture called D,L-panthenol. This
mixture has equal parts of two forms of the molecule, known as D and L, which are mirror
images of each other. D-panthenol is active in the body, while L-panthenol is not. D,L-
panthenol is a combination of both forms.

Since D-panthenol is biologically active, it is absorbed and converted into pantothenic acid
on the skin. D,L-panthenol has only half the activity of D-panthenol, but L-panthenol stays
on the skin and acts as a humectant.

D-panthenol is an odourless, yellowish-clear, viscous liquid, while D,L-panthenol is an
odourless, white crystalline powder. Both are soluble in water and alcohol and insoluble
in oil.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
It should be added to the cool-down phase of water-based formulations for skin, nail, and
hair care.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Panthenol should not be heated over 70ºC, as it may cause racemisation, which means
converting part of D-panthenol into the inactive L-panthenol.

High concentrations of panthenol may leave the formulation tacky.

name: Propanediol
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Propanediol is a natural glycol that can be produced through a corn sugar fermentation
process. It is a natural and greener alternative to petroleum-derived propylene glycol and
can be Cosmos and Ecocert-certified. It is an emollient and humectant, but it also works
as a preservative booster and solvent for other substances and plant extracts.

Propanediol helps restore the skin barrier function, stimulates ceramide synthesis, and
reduces transepidermal water loss.

CHARACTERISTICS
• Propanediol increases the clarity of surfactant systems.
   • It helps decrease skin water loss.
   • In hair care formulations, it increases moisturisation, reduces static and hair tangling,
     and gives a cleaner feeling.
   • Propanediol can be used to dissolve ingredients such as salicylic acid, ferulic acid,
     allantoin, and ascorbic acid.
   • Has a light, non-sticky feel on the skin.
   • It can be added to creams, lotions, shampoos, conditioners, sun care, and dry skin
     formulations.

COMPOSITION
Propanediol is a hygroscopic, water-soluble, clear, colourless and odourless, liquid. It is
very stable when heated, non-irritant, and non-sensitising.

It is often used in plant extracts as a solvent instead of glycerine because it has similar
properties but doesn't feel sticky on the skin. It also gives the extracts a smooth, pleasant
skin feel.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in water-based formulations as a humectant. It can be used in cleansing and haircare
formulations as well.

It can also be blended with gums instead of glycerine to make a slurry before dispersing the
gum in water, helping prevent the formation of clumps.

It works synergistically with glycerine for improved and extended skin moisturisation. Using
these ingredients together allows to reduce the concentration of glycerine, decreasing the
tackiness of the formulation

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
May have a synthetic or palm-derived origin; check with the supplier.

name: Sodium lactate
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Sodium lactate is the sodium salt of lactic acid and is used in cosmetics as a humectant
and buffering agent. It is found naturally on the skin and is part of its natural moisturising
factor (NMF). Due to its hygroscopic properties, it can absorb moisture from the
environment and keep it on the skin.

It is produced through the neutralisation of lactic acid produced from the fermentation of
corn or beet sugar.

CHARACTERISTICS
• Highly soluble in water.
   • When combined with alpha-hydroxy acids (AHAs), it increases their efficacy.
   • When present in amounts higher than 5% and in acidic conditions, it exhibits
     keratolytic properties.
   • Can be used to help keep the formulation’s pH stable.
   • Can be added to all kinds of formulations and is especially beneficial for those
     designed for dry skin.
   • In hair care formulations, it conditions the hair shaft, reduces frizz, and improves
     combability.

COMPOSITION
Sodium lactate is a colourless, odourless, clear liquid with a high heat tolerance. It is safe
and usually non-irritant or sensitising to human skin and scalp since it is naturally part of
the NMF.

Sodium lactate is highly hygroscopic and, when compared to glycerine, it is a more
effective moisturiser and gives a less sticky feeling to the formulation.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Add it to the water phase of the formulation.

Can be used as a pH buffer in formulations along with lactic acid, helping to keep the pH
stable and avoid pH drifts.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Even though it is usually non-irritant to the skin, individual sensitivities can appear.

Sodium lactate is a salt and can destabilise electrolyte-sensitive gums and emulsifiers.

name: Olivem 1000
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
This non-ionic oil-in-water emulsifier is derived from natural olive chemistry. It is an
emulsifier and thickener compatible with various cosmetic and active ingredients over
a wide pH range (4.5 to 8). It is safe and clinically tested to be hypoallergenic.
Olivem 1000 provides creams with excellent spreadability.

CHARACTERISTICS
We recommend this emulsifier if you are new to emulsions. It is easy to use as it doesn’t
require expensive equipment. It is a PEG-free O/W emulsifier and thickener that has the
ability to form liquid crystal structures that mimic the organisation of the lipids on the
stratum corneum. So, it helps improve the skin barrier function.

Furthermore, it provides a moisturising effect with good spreadability.

Olivem 1000 also has a unique ability to replace the oil phase in your emulsions
completely.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in facial and body creams or lotions, hand and foot care and other emulsified
products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It has an inherent soaping effect that can be reduced with a co-emulsifier (such as glyceryl
stearate) or a fatty alcohol (such as cetyl, cetearyl or brassica alcohol). Using
high-spreadability esters also can help diminish soaping.

The use of a stabiliser such as xanthan gum is recommended to increase viscosity and
improve the stability of Olivem 1000 emulsions.

name: Olivem 2090
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Olivem 2090 is a cold process W/O emulsifier derived from olive oil chemistry.
Olivem 2090 combines polyglycerol esters of olive oil fatty acids with polyricinoleic
acid, providing excellent emulsifying performance, a light sensory profile, and hydration
benefits.

CHARACTERISTICS
• This ingredient is a light-yellow viscous liquid with a faint odour.
   • Olivem 2090 can be used in a variety of W/O formulations such as cold creams,
     nappy, hand and foot creams, and winter formulations. Since W/O emulsions create
     a protective barrier on the skin’s surface, they help lock in moisture and are great
     for dry skin areas.
   • This emulsifier is versatile: it can accommodate a range of water phase content
     from 30% to 85% and is compatible with many kinds of preservatives.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use Olivem 2090 to create water-in-oil emulsions.

The amount of water-based ingredients included in the formulation will influence the texture
of the emulsion; the greater the water content, the richer the texture.

Adding electrolytes to your formulation helps stabilise W/O emulsions but can cause a pH
drift. Check and adjust the pH of the water phase before incorporating it into the oil phase.

Olivem 2090 is versatile and compatible with a wide range of oils, regardless of their
differing polarities.

The best thickener choices are hydrogenated castor oil, hydrophilic fumed silica, and Olivem
900 (INCI: Sorbitan Olivate).

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
W/o emulsions need more vigorous homogenisation to create a stable final product,
especially when working with cold-process emulsifiers. Make sure to check the emulsion’s
stability.

Chelators must be avoided in W/O emulsions, as they may interact with the electrolytes used
as stabilisers.

name: Vegetal
function: Emulsifying Other trading names                      SugarMulse, Glucomulse, Montanov68, Emulgade PL 68/50
colour: Ivory to light yellow waxy pastilles
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
It is a 100 % vegetable derived non-ionic O/W emulsifier made from the fatty alcohols of
coconut or palm oil and the glucose from corn, wheat, or cassava. It is available as ivory,
solid pellets.

Vegetal creates emulsions with minimal soapiness. Furthermore, it is able to form a liquid
crystal structure that helps improve the skin barrier function, providing a long-lasting
moisturising effect and reducing transepidermal water loss (TEWL).

CHARACTERISTICS
It can be used as a standalone emulsifier or as a co-emulsifier to other O/W emulsifiers.

By varying the oil-emulsifier ratio, you can create emulsions of various viscosities.

According to the manufacturer, this emulsifier can handle a wide pH range between 3 – 12.

It provides a long-lasting moisturising effect with good spreadability.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in facial and body creams or lotions, hand and foot care and other emulsified
products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
High shear is recommended in the first stage of the emulsification process. However, after
the emulsion is formed, only a gentle stir should be applied as a high shear could destroy the
liquid crystal structure, leading to phase separation.

name: Lecithin
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Lecithin is a by-product of the soy and sunflower oil extraction process (we recommend
liquid sunflower lecithin).

It is a mixture of lipid substances: Its main components are phospholipids, such as
phosphatidylcholine, but it may also contain fatty acids, triglycerides, sterols, and
glycolipids. Phospholipids are present in the cell membranes of plants, animals, and
marine organisms, so lecithin is highly biocompatible. The phospholipids' composition
may vary according to the lecithin source and extraction methods.

Lecithin is an amphoteric emulsifier and thickener used to make W/O emulsions, but that
also works in O/W emulsions. It works as an emollient, refatting agent and prevents skin
water loss. It is a very moisturising ingredient.

CHARACTERISTICS
It makes balms and butters very creamy, even if you use only small amounts. Add it to oil-
containing products.

It can be tricky to work with and will require lots of practice.

As W/O emulsions tend to feel richer on the skin, not everyone loves it, but still, it can be a
great product for a niche.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in lip balms, haircare, anhydrous creams, balms, butters, oils, and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It has a characteristic aroma and strong colour. Consider this when using it in formulations.

name: Sapogel q
inci: Glycerin (and) Aqua (and) Quillaja saponaria Wood Extract (and)
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Sapogel Q is a blend of naturally derived saponins. It works as an oil-gelling agent for
plant oils and is used to create oleogels with consistencies varying from fluid gels to
balm-like. This ingredient is one of the possible choices when creating self-emulsifying
oleogels (gel-to-milk), which will turn into a milky texture when it comes in contact with
water, making it easier to wash off.

CHARACTERISTICS
Creating self-emulsifying oleogels is a great way to enhance the sensory experience of
using vegetable oils. Sapogel Q is suitable for both rinse-off and leave-on formulations,
such as cleansers, masks, massage gels, shave gels, scrubs, and exfoliants.

When solubilised in water, this oil-to-milk emulsifier forms a lamellar structure with oil and
water/glycerine layers. This is how it turns into a milky texture when washed off and why
adding water-based ingredients to the formulations may leave them more opaque.

Even though Sapogel Q is particularly suited to gelling vegetable oils, which are usually
slightly polar, most non-polar oils (such as squalane) can also be gelled. Butters can be
mixed with it without crystals forming.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Sapogel Q is an oil-gelling agent with self-emulsifying properties that can be used in
oleogels and oil-to-milk formulations.

When formulating with this ingredient, the less you use, the thicker and firmer the oleogel
will be, while using Sapogel Q in high quantities will result in a more fluid consistency.

If you're aiming for a fluid texture but want to use lower amounts of Sapogel Q, adding
glycerine to your formulation is a good option.

Sapogel Q can accommodate up to 4% of water-based ingredients in the formulations.
Remember that those ingredients will produce a more opaque and fluid oleogel with a
creamy texture.

Sapogel Q can be processed at room temperature unless waxes or butters are used in the
formula. If that is the case, melt them into the oil phase first.

Before adding the oils to Sapogel Q, you must stir it until it turns opaque, which indicates it
is ready to be used.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
When formulating, all the oily ingredients should be mixed until thoroughly combined, then
they must be added little by little to the gelling agent. You must ensure that all the oil is
fully incorporated before adding more; this will ensure your formulation is stable and has
the right texture.

Polar oils tend to make oleogels more viscous, while non-polar oils will result in runnier
formulations. This is due to the interaction of these different types of oils with the gelling
agent.

High amounts of non-polar oils can affect the stability of oleogels made with Sapogel Q.

Non-polar oils tend to make oleogels clearer, while polar oils make more opaque ones.

name: Sucragel aof bio
inci: Glycerin (and) Prunus Amygdalus Dulcis (Sweet Almond) Oil (and)
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Sucragel AOF Bio is a 100% natural, preservative-free, oil thickening and emulsifying
ingredient derived from sugar and coconut.

CHARACTERISTICS
It can be used as a liquid emulsifier for cold or hot processed oil-in-water (O/W)
emulsions.

It has foam boosting properties. It can be used on its own or combined with another
surfactant for gentle and mild cleansing.

You can use it with plant oils to create oleogels, which will turn into a milky liquid when
in contact with water. That is called gel-to-milk technology. These can be cold processed
and are capable of forming clear to translucent oleogels. For thicker oleogels, especially
those suspending exfoliating particles, the use of Sucrablend SP V2 as a stabiliser is
recommended.

It is a good ingredient for cleansing products, facial polishes or even body scrubs. Alone,
the oleogels can be used as moisturisers or even as cuticle and nail gels.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it as an O/W emulsifier or with plant oils to create oleogels. For making oleogels,
remember to be patient, add the oils very slowly and mix well before adding more.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Can be challenging to work with as an O/W emulsifier. We recommend this emulsifier only
for those with emulsification experience.

For making oleogels, you can use a spatula or glass rod for hand blending or use the
dough hook of your electric whisk. Remember to add the oils slowly to create a stable
formulation.

The supplier recommends pairing it with Sucrablend SP V2 to stabilise formulations
processed at temperatures above 40 °C (104 °F).

name: Polyaquol 2w
inci: Polyglyceryl-2 Stearate (and) Glyceryl Stearate (and) Stearyl Alcohol
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
PolyAquol 2W is a non-ionic, PEG-free and naturally derived O/W emulsifier. Even though it
is not palm oil-free, it has an RSPO certification, which operates to make sustainable palm
oil the norm.

PolyAquol 2W is a versatile emulsifier that is easy to use. It possesses a wide range of
formulation compatibility while providing a unique skin feel to emulsions. It can be used to
create emulsions with low viscosity or rich creams.

This emulsifier acts as a repairing, protective and moisturising agent. It protects and
repairs the skin barrier, preventing UV-induced skin dehydration.

In addition, it generates liquid crystal structures that may help deliver active ingredients
into the skin layers while providing the skin with long-lasting hydration. These lamellar-
structured emulsions also have excellent stability.

CHARACTERISTICS
PolyAquol 2W emulsifies oils up to a 1:4 ratio without the need for thickeners and has
self-emulsifying properties. This ability to self-emulsify in water to form a stable system
means this emulsifier can be used to create products without an oil phase (for example,
creamy cleansing products).

PolyAquol 2W is a very easy emulsifier to work with and is suitable for lower oil
concentrations, from 5% to 20%. It can be added to either the water or the oil phase of an
emulsion and can be heated to 75 – 85ºC. The viscosity of the emulsion is higher when
PolyAquol 2W is added to the oil phase and lower when added to the water phase.

PolyAquol 2W is tolerant towards electrolytes (table salt -> NaCl) up to 3%. That is very
uncommon, since O/W emulsions normally break with the addition of salts.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it to create emulsions and cleansing products for skincare, haircare, baby care,
after-sun products, and make-up.

name: Xyliance
inci: Cetearyl Wheat Straw Glycosides (and) Cetearyl Alcohol
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Xyliance is a classic hot-process non-ionic emulsifier that can create silky, non-greasy and
non-soapy emulsions. Xyliance used to be palm-free, but this is not the case any more
(since 2015).

CHARACTERISTICS
Xyliance is a hot process emulsifier, which creates medium to high viscosity emulsions
and creams. It doesn’t work well at low oil concentrations and is not suitable to create low
viscosity emulsions or sprayable milks.

Emulsions created with xyliance are luxurious and fluffy. They are usually white or off-
white unless you incorporate oils with a distinct colour like açai or sea buckthorn oil.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in hand and body creams, rich facial creams, masques, and haircare products such
as deep conditioners and masks with high oil concentrations.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
With low batch volumes, you can create stable emulsions without a homogeniser.
However, Xyliance is an emulsifier that likes high shear. Give preference to using a Dynamix
homogeniser (the replacement for the infamous Kai Blendia) or a professional rotor/stator
homogeniser, as they improve the stability and texture of the emulsions.

Like many other oil-in-water emulsions, this emulsifier has a low electrolyte (salt) tolerance
and the emulsions made with Xyliance break upon the addition of salts.

Xyliance works even without applying a gum, but the long-term stability is much better
when adding a viscosity modifier (a gum) and/or an emulsion stabiliser.

name: Carrageenan
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Carrageenan is an anionic polymer based on sulphated polysaccharides. It is extracted
from red algae (Rhodophyceae), mainly Irish moss (Chondrus crispus). Most commonly
sold as an odourless off-white powder, carrageenan is used primarily as a thickening and
stabilising ingredient with film-forming, viscosity controlling and binding properties.

There are various types of carrageenan, which impart different properties to cosmetic
products. Usually, carrageenan gels are hydrating to the skin and help discipline the hair,
as they provide antistatic activity.

CHARACTERISTICS
There are different types of carrageenan, mainly kappa, iota and lambda, which differ in
their degree of sulphation. Kappa and iota carrageenans form thermo-reversible gels.
Typically, carrageenans are sold as stabilised salts of sodium, potassium, or calcium.

Kappa carrageenan forms rigid and brittle gels in the presence of potassium ions. It can
present syneresis, an undesired phenomenon in which the gel expels part of the liquid.
It works in synergy with xanthan gum, which helps to create gels that are more elastic
and cohesive.

Iota carrageenan forms elastic and transparent gels in the presence of calcium ions.
It does not present syneresis and is the most interesting type for cosmetic use.

Lambda carrageenan is not a gelling agent, but forms viscous solutions in water.

They work well within a pH between 6 – 9 and are compatible with anionic, amphoteric
and non-ionic surfactants.

Kappa and iota carrageenan are only soluble in hot water at temperatures above 60 °C (140 °F).
Disperse them first in cold water before heating them while stirring.

Carrageenan can create gels with different viscosities, so don’t be afraid to experiment.
Try 0.5% first in distilled water to see how it behaves. Increase the amount gradually, take
photos and notes to remind yourself which ratio worked well.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in gels, emulsions, and haircare products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Blend the gum with glycerine before dispersing it in cold water to prevent the formation of
clumps. You can also use a high shear mixer such as an overhead stirrer or a blender to
disperse the gum.

There are some concerns regarding the safety of carrageenan. However, this comes
from studies where it is used in its degraded form or injected subcutaneously to induce
inflammation. The topical use of cosmetic grade carrageenan is considered safe and should
not cause any concern.

name: Gum arabic
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Gum arabic, also known as acacia gum, is a natural gum made from the hardened sap
of two species of acacia tree. These are grown commercially throughout the Sahel, from
Somalia to Senegal, although they were traditionally harvested in the Middle East and
West Asia.

Gum arabic is an off-white to beige, free-flowing, light-weight, granular powder. In
cosmetics, it provides adhesive and stabilising properties, but does not present good
gelling properties. It dissolves in water and binds to lipid particles, which means it has
limited emulsification properties.

This gum is considered a natural “tightening” agent, which helps to improve the
appearance of wrinkles, but only as a transitory effect.

Commonly used in traditional medicine as a soothing and anti-inflammatory agent, this
mixture of anionic polysaccharides and glycoproteins has good water solubility.

CHARACTERISTICS
Gum arabic will not make thick gels as you would see with other thickeners. It is used more
often in colour cosmetics, such as in mascaras.

This gum is dispersible in an aqueous base. It is known for its strong ability to adhere to
hydrophobic liquids and solids (which do not like water), hence its usefulness as a cohesive
agent in emulsions. It can help with emulsion stability and, in skincare products, it creates
a thin layer on the skin, reducing dehydration.

Gum arabic must be dispersed in cold water and then heated to 70ºC until fully solubilised.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in lotions, creams, and make-up.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It will not create viscous gels.

name: Gum tragacanth
function: Binding, emulsion stabilising, film forming, fragrance, viscosity controlling
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Tragacanth is a natural anionic gum obtained from the dried sap of several Middle Eastern
legume species of the Astragalus genus.

Gum tragacanth is a viscous, odourless, tasteless, water-soluble polysaccharides' mixture
obtained from the sap drained from the plant roots and dried. The gum also seeps from
the plant in twisted ribbons or flakes, which can also be powdered.

CHARACTERISTICS
This gum can be used to thicken the water phase of emulsions, helping stabilise them.

Gum tragacanth swells rapidly in either cold or hot water to form highly viscous colloids or
partial gels, which act as protective colloids and stabilising agents for your formulations.

Start with a low percentage when testing out new formulations.

It has good acid resistance, but it is better to add acids after the gum is fully hydrated.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in gels, O/W emulsions and hairstyling products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Blend the gum with glycerine before dispersing it in cold water to prevent the formation of
clumps. You can also use a high shear mixer such as an overhead stirrer or a blender to
disperse the gum.

Tragacanth is prone to microbiological contamination, even in the presence of
preservatives.

If used in shower gels or shampoos, it should not be combined with cationic surfactants,
as this would cause the gel structure to break.

Because of its high price, tragacanth gum is not often used in cosmetic products.

name: Guar gum
function: Binding, emulsion stabilising, film forming, fragrance, viscosity controlling
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Guar gum is a non-ionic thickener obtained by grinding the seeds of Cyamopsis
tetragonolobus, a legume native to India and Pakistan. It is an off-white to yellowish
powder with a faint characteristic odour.

This gum is mainly composed of polysaccharides such as galactomannan and can be
dissolved in hot and cold water. It is considered a gentle ingredient compatible with most
skin types.

CHARACTERISTICS
Guar gum has the ability to hydrate rapidly in cold water and produce highly viscous
solutions.

It can also be used in emulsified lotions and creams as a protective colloid, increasing
emulsion stability and preventing water loss.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in facial gels and emulsions, shower gels, shampoos, coloured cosmetics,
and toothpaste.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Some find the natural aroma of guar quite unpleasant.

It is recommended to combine it with xanthan gum as this reduces the amount of both
gums and creates a more satisfactory feel.

name: Konjac
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Konjac gum is a polysaccharide made out of the tuber of Amorphophallus konjac. It is
an odourless white powder with the ability to form a clear, transparent gel. It has great
thickening properties and good stability.

It is used in the food industry as well as the cosmetics industry. Konjac gum works in
a wide range of temperatures and pH (4 – 10).

It creates a less sticky and creamier consistency than guar gum while providing a thin
protective layer on the skin, helping to restore moisture.

CHARACTERISTICS
You can create a synergistic blend with carrageenan and xanthan gum.

Alone, it creates a transparent gel with a lovely skin feel. It works well as an emulsion
stabiliser, and it doesn’t form the lumps that xanthan is notorious for.

Use it to create gels, approx. 1% would give a thick gel. Using hot water will speed up the
thickening process. In creams and lotions, 0.05 – 0.2% would be sufficient for stability.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in skincare products and haircare (shampoos).

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Blend the gum with glycerine before dispersing it in cold water to prevent the formation of
clumps. You can also use a high shear mixer such as an overhead stirrer or a blender to
disperse the gum.

name: Sclerotium gum
function: Emulsion stabiliser, skin conditioning, viscosity controlling
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Sclerotium gum is a non-ionic polymer, also known as scleroglucan. It is a polysaccharide
obtained through aerobic fermentation of glucose by fungi from the genus Sclerotium.

This gum is able to produce translucent gels and can be used as a stabiliser for emulsions
and suspensions. It presents good stability at high temperatures (up to 70ºC) and a wide
pH range.

It forms a protective film over the skin, helping to keep it hydrated.

CHARACTERISTICS
This natural gum produces gels with outstanding properties. It is not sticky and tacky like
other gums such as xanthan, presenting a silkier and smoother skin feel.

The viscosity of sclerotium gels increases with temperature and becomes even higher
when used in synergy with xanthan gum.

Because of its non-ionic nature, sclerotium gum is stable through a wide pH range from
pH 3 – 12. It is compatible with acids, alkalis, and electrolytes and can be used to thicken
surfactant systems.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in gels, emulsions, scrubs, shower gels, shampoos, and other haircare products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Blend the gum with glycerine before dispersing it in cold water to prevent the formation
of clumps. You can also use a high shear mixer such as an overhead stirrer or a blender
to disperse the gum. If you disperse it in cold water, you might need to leave it resting
overnight until fully hydrated.

name: Solagum ax
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Solagum AX is a natural thickening and stabilising, water-soluble polymer. This blend
of acacia gum and xanthan gum dissolves quickly in hot or cold water, and delivers
outstanding skin feel with a non-stringy, non-sticky & fresh aqueous sensation.

It forms clear aqueous gels and has good particle suspension power. Solagum AX is
stable at a wide pH range (3 – 12) and is compatible with solvents, surfactants and
alpha-hydroxy acids. It forms clear aqueous gels with excellent skin tolerance (good for
sensitive/intimate areas).

CHARACTERISTICS
It forms low to medium viscosity gels, and you can create a synergistic blend with other
gums if needed.

Furthermore, it works well as an emulsion stabiliser, also helping increase the viscosity of
shampoos and shower gels.

Use it in shower gels and shampoos, or to stabilise creams and lotions. It has excellent
resistance to electrolytes.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in facial and body care, after-sun care, haircare, make-up, shower gels, and cleansers.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Blend the gum with glycerine before dispersing it in cold water to prevent the formation of
clumps. You can also use a high shear mixer such as an overhead stirrer or a blender to
disperse the gum.

name: Xanthan gum
function: Binding, emulsion stabilising, gel forming, skin conditioning, surfactant – cleansing and emulsifying, viscosity controlling
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Xanthan gum is an anionic polymer formed by polysaccharides (sugar) secreted by the
bacterium Xanthomonas campestris. It is frequently found in food as a thickening agent
and used in cosmetics as a thickener and stabiliser, where it helps prevent emulsions
from separating.

It is produced by the fermentation of glucose, sucrose, or lactose solutions. After a
fermentation period, the polymer is precipitated with isopropyl alcohol, dried, and ground
into a fine odourless powder.

CHARACTERISTICS
Xanthan gum can be purchased in two forms, transparent and non-clear. They both work
well on aqueous bases, and the difference will be mainly aesthetic.

Xanthan gum can remain stable within a wide pH range (3 – 12). It is compatible with
ethanol and anionic, amphoteric and non-ionic surfactants, but not with cationic ones, as
it would create an unstable product.

Like other gums, it is best blended with glycerine first and then added to the water to avoid
clumping. If you don't use glycerine, try to create a vortex first and sprinkle the gum into it.
This is best done with a magnetic stirrer, but can also be done using a glass rod.

In emulsions, this gum can either be blended in glycerine or dispersed in the oil phase
(it will not solubilise until the addition to the water phase).

Gels created with xanthan tend to thicken a bit more over time.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in gels, emulsions, scrubs, shower gels, and shampoos.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Heat will help xanthan gum to form homogenous gels.

name: Cetearyl alcohol
function: Emollient, emulsifying, viscosity controlling, emulsion stabilising
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Cetearyl alcohol, sometimes called cetostearyl alcohol, is a mix of cetyl and stearyl
alcohols. Usually, it is found as a blend of 30% cetyl alcohol and 70% stearyl alcohol, but it
can be found at different ratios depending on the supplier.

Fatty alcohols, such as cetearyl alcohol, are emollients for the skin and are used in
cosmetic formulations as co-emulsifiers, fatty thickeners, emulsion stabilisers, and
viscosity-controlling agents.

Cetearyl alcohol is obtained by the reduction of palmitic and stearic acids from vegetable
triglycerides.

CHARACTERISTICS
• Cetearyl alcohol is frequently used as a co-emulsifier and helps stabilise the
         emulsion’s texture and consistency. It is part of some emulsifying blends, such as
         Vegetal and Xyliance, also covered in this Ingredients Directory.

   • It improves the texture of formulations, making them smoother and less sticky
     when compared to those containing waxes. It can also be used to substitute part of
     the heavy emollients in a formulation, such as butters and waxes, maintaining the
     formulation’s moisturising potential and body, while improving its overall texture.
   • It can be added to creams, lotions, body washes, exfoliants, and hair care
     formulations.
   • In haircare, it increases spreadability, which allows the formulations to glide
     through hair.
   • Even though it is an alcohol, it has an oil-soluble carbon chain and doesn’t present
     the drying effect often associated with alcohols such as ethanol.
   • Cetearyl alcohol is biodegradable and non-bioaccumulative.

COMPOSITION
Cetearyl alcohol is an oil-soluble, white, wax-like substance usually found as flakes or
pellets. The mix of stearyl and cetyl alcohols gives this fatty alcohol unique properties
such as better heat tolerance, improved stability, and the formation of a better lamellar gel
network. It is considered non-irritant and non-sensitising.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Can be added to O/W and W/O emulsions, haircare, and anhydrous formulations.

Heat cetearyl alcohol to melt it or add it to the heated oil phase of the formulation.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
If not completely dissolved into the oil phase, cetearyl alcohol can cause graininess in the
final formulation.

Concentrations higher than 1.5% in facial formulations may cause a skin feeling of
sweating.

name: Cetyl alcohol
function: Emollient, emulsifying, viscosity controlling, emulsion stabilising
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Cetyl alcohol is a common ingredient found in cosmetic formulations like creams and
lotions. It is a fatty alcohol (long-chain alcohol), which means it has an alcohol group
(-OH) attached to a carbon tail. This chemical structure is responsible for its emollient and
co-emulsifying properties. It also works as an oil thickener and viscosity enhancer.
Cetyl alcohol works as an emollient and helps keep the skin moisturised.

Cetyl alcohol is usually sourced from coconut or palm kernel oil.

CHARACTERISTICS
• Cetyl alcohol works as a co-emulsifier and stabilises emulsions, helping prevent
     water and oil from separating.
   • In anhydrous formulations such as lipsticks, lotion bars, balms, shampoo and
     conditioner bars, it hardens the formulations and enhances their texture. In
     lipsticks, it helps the colour adhere to the lips.

   • Can be added to creams, lotions, body washes, exfoliants, and hair care
       formulations.

   • In haircare, it increases spreadability, which allows the formulation to glide through
     hair.
   • It improves the texture of formulations, making them smoother and less sticky when
     compared to waxes.
   • It is considered non-irritant and non-sensitising, and like all other fatty alcohols,
     it has an oil-soluble carbon chain and doesn’t present the drying effect often
     associated with alcohols such as ethanol.

COMPOSITION
Cetyl alcohol is an oil-soluble, white, wax-like substance usually found as flakes or pellets.
In oil-in-water emulsions, such as creams, this ingredient helps stabilise the formulation,
increase viscosity, and enhance the texture of the final product. Due to its unique
crystalline structure, cetyl alcohol produces a lighter, less viscous texture in water-in-oil
(w/o) emulsions compared to other fatty thickeners.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Can be added to O/W and W/O emulsions, haircare, and anhydrous formulations.

Heat cetearyl alcohol to melt it or add it to the heated oil phase of the formulation.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Even though it is considered non-irritant, some people with extra-sensitive skin may show
irritation signs, mainly due to impurities in the ingredient.

name: Stearic acid
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Stearic acid is a saturated long-chain fatty acid present in our sebum and found as a
primary component in shea and cocoa butter and other plant oils and butters, from which
it is usually extracted via hydrolysis. It is used in cosmetics as a co-emulsifier, fatty
thickener, emollient agent, and skin barrier protectant.

Check the stearic acid’s origin with the supplier, as some may come from synthetic or
animal-derived sources.

CHARACTERISTICS
• Stearic acid has multiple beneficial properties. It is an excellent co-emulsifier and
     emulsion stabiliser, helping keep oil- and water-based ingredients together while
     giving the formulation a luxurious sensory profile.
   • As a fatty acid, it is incorporated into the lipid layer of the skin and improves its
     barrier function while reducing transepidermal water loss, leaving a moisturising
     effect.

   • When mixed into liquid oils, it gives them a more buttery consistency and skin feel.
   • When used in cleansing balms or body scrubs, it thickens the formulation while
     maintaining an easy rinse-off characteristic.
   • When using stearic acid, it is possible to use less wax, which improves the
     formulation's skin feel.
   • It is a stronger thickener than cetyl and cetearyl alcohol; therefore, the final product
     will be firmer if you substitute one of them for stearic acid.
   • Stearic acid can be added to creams, lotions, hair care formulations, cleansers, body
     washes, and scrubs. conditioner bars, it hardens the formulations and enhances
     their texture. In lipsticks, it helps the colour adhere to the lips.

COMPOSITION
Stearic acid is a white-to-yellowish, waxy solid found in flakes, beads, or powder form. It
has an oil-like odour and is soluble in oil, with good heat stability. It is considered safe
and can be used on all skin types, even though some sensitive skins may find it slightly
irritating.

It is a natural, safe, and biodegradable ingredient with many functions in cosmetic
formulations.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Should be heated until melted or added to the heated oil phase of the formulation.

Can be added to emulsions, haircare, and anhydrous formulations.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Avoid using it in formulations with a high pH.

Can be slightly irritating for sensitive skin types.

name: Cocamidopropyl betaine
function: Antistatic, cleansing, foam boosting, hair conditioning, surfactant, viscosity controlling
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Cocamidopropyl betaine (CAPB) is a mild amphoteric surfactant that presents both
anionic and cationic charges (depending on the pH of the formulation), providing
cleansing and conditioning properties.

It is mainly derived from coconut oil, but it can be derived from palm oil as well, so check
with your supplier to see if the product is palm-free.

It is very gentle and suitable for all cleansing products, especially baby products and mild
facial cleansers.

CHARACTERISTICS
This surfactant has an antistatic and hair conditioning function. It also helps to increase
and stabilise foam, regulate the viscosity and enhance the mildness of some surfactant
blends.

It is often used as a secondary surfactant, which means it should be blended with other
surfactants in the formula for best results, although it also works as a sole surfactant.

CAPB is compatible with anionic, cationic, non-ionic, and other amphoteric surfactants.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in haircare and facial cleansing products, micellar waters, shower gels and baby
cleansing products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It can be a watery or viscous liquid.

It has a salt content (NaCl) of max. 6.0%

Some people have reported an allergic reaction when using products containing
cocamidopropyl betaine. However, studies found that it is not the ingredient
itself that causes allergic reactions, but two impurities (aminoamide and
3-dimethylaminopropylamine) that are produced in the manufacturing process. It seems
that manufacturers are aware of this and are minimising the content of these by-products,
helping to reduce skin sensitisation reports related to CAPB.

name: Coco-glucoside
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Coco-glucoside is a mild non-ionic surfactant that belongs to the class of alkyl glucosides
and is derived from coconut fatty alcohols and glucose from sugar or starch. It is a cloudy,
viscous and pale-yellow liquid.

CHARACTERISTICS
This surfactant has good foaming and cleansing properties, yet it is mild and gentle,
making it a good choice for products directed to sensitive skin. It can be used on its own
or combined with other surfactants for gentle and mild cleansing.

Coco-glucoside has foam stabilising, viscosity boosting and skin conditioning abilities,
and it could be used as the main surfactant or as a co-surfactant.

Coco-glucoside is compatible with anionic, cationic, amphoteric, and other non-ionic
surfactants.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in haircare and facial cleansing products, micellar waters, shower gels and baby
cleansing products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It does have a high pH, so make sure you adjust the pH of the final product.

name: Decyl glucoside
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Decyl glucoside is another mild non-ionic surfactant from the class of alkyl glucosides.
It is derived from plant-based fatty alcohols (mainly coconut or palm) and glucose from
sugar or starch.

Decyl glucoside has mainly C10 carbon chain length, but can be a mixture of C8 – C16.
It has a superior solubility compared to coco glucoside or lauryl glucoside.

CHARACTERISTICS
It creates a good and stable foam for a non-ionic surfactant. However, its touch is not
comparable to the foam of anionic surfactants. For this reason, you can combine it with
cocamidopropyl betaine or natural anionic surfactants to enhance the smoothness of the
foam. It also has conditioning properties.

It is particularly good for shower gels and bath products. Furthermore, it has a high water
solubility even at reduced temperatures, making it useful for micellar water formulations.

Decyl glucoside can be used on its own or combined with other surfactants for gentle and
mild cleansing. It is fully compatible with anionic, cationic, amphoteric, and other non-
ionic surfactants, so it is worth experimenting with various combinations.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in haircare and facial cleansing products, micellar waters, shower gels and baby
cleansing products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It does have a high pH, so make sure you adjust the pH of the final product.

In products directed to very dry skin, adding a refatting ingredient such as the mixture of
coco-glucoside/glyceryl oleate can help to reduce any potential irritation.

name: Scs (sodium coco sulfate)
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Sodium coco sulphate (SCS) is an anionic surfactant derived from coconut fatty acids.
It is usually found in needle or powder form. It cleanses the skin and hair and helps create
a rich foam.

SCS is similar to sodium lauryl sulphate (SLS), as they both originate from coconut or
palm oil. However, they differ a little in their manufacturing processes. SLS is produced
using isolated lauric acid from these oils, while SCS is made from whole coconut or
palm oil.

Although many people think this ingredient is not natural because of “free from sulphates”
product claims and similarities with SLES (INCI: Sodium Laureth Sulfate), an ethoxylated
surfactant, SCS is accepted by Cosmos and can be used in natural formulations. However,
like other sulphates, it is a harsh surfactant that should be used sparingly.

CHARACTERISTICS
SCS can be incorporated into shower bars, shampoos, shower gels, and other cleansing
formulations. It acts by removing oil and impurities from the skin and hair. It is a gentler
and greener alternative to SLES, but still a strong surfactant.

In shower bars and solid shampoos, solid surfactants, such as SCS, also help harden the
formulation, allowing it to hold its shape.

Unlike the manufacturing of sodium lauryl sulphate, SCS keeps the high molecular weight
fatty acids of coconut oil, which makes the foam produced denser and gives a more
conditioning feel to the skin after use. It is particularly good for shower gels and bath
products. Furthermore, it has a high water solubility even at reduced temperatures, making
it useful for micellar water formulations.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
It can be used to formulate anhydrous cosmetics, haircare, and water-based cleansing
formulations.

Liquid cleansers made with SCS typically have denser, creamier foam.

If you use the cold method to produce shower bars, it should be mixed with the other
powdered ingredients.

If you are formulating shower bars using the hot process, all surfactants must be mixed and
heated to around 80º C until they form a paste. This must be made in slow, steady heat and
gently mixed; high shear mixing will make it too thick to work with.

It is water-soluble and, in liquid formulations, should be added to the heated water phase.

It does have a high pH of around 9, so make sure you adjust the pH of the final formulation.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Inhaling solid surfactants can result in irritation of the respiratory tract; therefore, wear a
safety mask when handling them.

SCS may irritate sensitive skin types, so it is advised to combine it with milder surfactants.

If you use SCS as a substitute for other surfactants, you may find it necessary to adapt the
quantities used.

name: SLSa (sodium lauryl sulfoacetate)
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Sodium lauryl sulfoacetate is a solid anionic surfactant that meets Ecocert and Cosmos
standards. It is water-soluble and is usually found as a very fine white powder. Though
its name may be similar to SLS (INCI: Sodium Lauryl Sulfate), they are not the same
ingredient, and SLSa is a gentler surfactant.

In formulations, it cleanses the skin and hair and creates a rich lather. SLSa comes in a
pH that ranges from 5 to 7.5 and can be mixed with other solid surfactants to obtain the
desired cleansing and good skin tolerance properties.

CHARACTERISTICS
SLSa has good cleansing properties without being too harsh; therefore, it is a good choice
for more sensitive skin types and baby formulations.

It can be incorporated into shower bars, shower gels, haircare formulations, and others.
It produces a creamy, rich, long-lasting lather, and is an excellent choice for bath bombs
and salts.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
It can be used to formulate shower bars, haircare and water-based formulations.

If you use the cold method to produce shower bars, it should be mixed with the other
powdered ingredients.

If you are formulating shower bars using the hot process, the surfactants must be mixed
and heated to around 80ºC until they form a paste.

In liquid formulations, it should be added to the heated water phase.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Inhaling solid surfactants can result in irritation of the respiratory tract; therefore, wear a
safety mask when handling it.

If you use SLSa as a substitute for other surfactants, you will find it necessary to adapt
the quantities used.

name: Sodium cocoyl isethionate (sci)
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Sodium cocoyl isethionate, also known by its acronym SCI, is a mild and high-foaming
anionic surfactant derived from coconut or palm oil fatty acids. It is presented in various
forms, such as powder, granules, flakes, or noodles. This surfactant can be used to create
solid cleansing products such as shampoo or shower bars. SCI is tolerant to hard water
and is biodegradable.

CHARACTERISTICS
SCI presents good foam density and stability and is a good choice for creating shower
and shampoo bars, shaving foams and other cleansing products.

It has a slightly acidic pH (between 5 – 6.5), which needs less or no adjustments in the
final product. One of its advantages is good tolerance to hard water, leaving no sediments
and not losing foaming. It benefits from being paired with amphoteric surfactants such as
cocamidopropyl betaine, which increases even more its mildness.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in shampoo and shower bars, shaving foams and other mild cleansing products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
This surfactant is not Ecocert, Natrue, or Cosmos certified, so keep this in mind if you
want to certify your products under any of those standards.

name: Sucrose cocoate
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Sucrose cocoate is a mild, non-ionic surfactant that is an ester derived from coconut fatty
acids and sugar. It is considered a hydrophilic emollient, which can help to increase the
foam density, creaminess, and viscosity when combined with other surfactants.

CHARACTERISTICS
Sucrose cocoate provides an improved skin feel during and after the washing process and
is considered a refatting agent. It is very mild and can be used in both leave-on and rinse-
off products. It has skin conditioning properties and can increase foam creaminess and
stability when combined with other surfactants.

This surfactant is sold as a white to yellowish paste. It is compatible with anionic,
cationic, amphoteric, and other non-ionic surfactants.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in haircare and facial cleansing products, micellar waters, shower gels, moisturisers,
and baby cleansing products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It is a thick paste at room temperature. For better processing, it can be heated at
40 – 60 °C (104 – 140 °F) in a water bath or added to water at 65 – 70 °C (149 – 158 °F) before being added to
the formulation.

name: Quillaja extract
inci: Quillaja Saponaria Bark Extract or Quillaja Saponaria Wood Extract
function: Anti-seborrheic, cleansing, foaming, fragrance, moisturising, skin conditioning, surfactant – cleansing and emulsifying
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Quillaja extract is derived from the tree with the same name that grows only in the desert
areas of Chile (Quillaja saponaria). Its parts, mostly the bark and wood, have a high
triterpenoid saponin content (which belong to the non-ionic group of surfactants).

CHARACTERISTICS
This extract has low foaming abilities. While it can be used alone, it presents better
foaming when coupled with other surfactants such as coco-glucoside, while also helping
to increase the mildness of the product.

It is a light brown, odourless liquid, but is also available in powder form.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in cleansing products such as foams, shampoos, shower gels, makeup removers,
and others.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects are known.

name: Yucca liquid extract
inci: Yucca Schidigera Stem Extract or Yucca Schidigera Leaf/Root/Stem Extract
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Yucca liquid extract is made from the juice of the plant stem, which is cold-pressed and
concentrated to approximately 50% of water content, which is then filtered, pasteurised,
and preserved. The process doesn’t use any solvents or carriers.

The extract contains steroid saponins together with polyphenols such as resveratrol.

CHARACTERISTICS
Yucca extract works as a surfactant because it contains saponins (which belong to the
non-ionic group of surfactants). It can be used as a primary surfactant, co-surfactant, or
as a co-emulsifier and emulsion stabiliser.

Yucca extract is water-soluble and has a pH of about 3.8.

It is compatible with anionic, cationic, amphoteric, and other non-ionic surfactants. It is
best to use it in low concentrations due to its expensive price and intense caramel colour.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in cleansing products such as foams, shampoos, shower gels, and makeup removers.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It has an intense colour and earthy aroma. Best used at low percentages.

name: Symbio solv clear plus mb
inci: Caprylyl/Capryl Glucoside (and) Aqua (and) Sodium Cocoyl Glutamate (and)
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Symbio Solv Clear Plus MB is a solubiliser blend derived from natural sources, composed
of surfactants and wetting agents. It allows the incorporation of small amounts of light
oil-soluble ingredients, such as essential oils, in water-based formulations. It is a viscous,
light yellow, and almost odourless liquid.

CHARACTERISTICS
This solubiliser yields transparent solutions and gives a pleasant, non-sticky feel to the
formulation. It contributes to the foaming performance of cleansing formulations and is
suitable for alcohol-containing and alcohol-free products. Symbio Solv Clear Plus MB is
used in low dosages due to the low concentration needed to form micelles and shows
good solubilising performance. It can be used in toners, micellar waters, body washes,
gels, foams, and other water-based formulations. It also helps remove makeup from
the skin.

Solubilisers can also be used to incorporate some preservatives with oil-soluble
components into a water-based formulation.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
It can be used in water- and surfactant-based formulations, with or without alcohol.

At room temperature, pre-mix Symbio Solv Clear Plus MB with the essential oils or
preservatives that need to be solubilised. Then, gradually add this mixture to the aqueous
phase while stirring.

The final formulation should have a pH range of 4.5 - 6.5.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Incompatible with cationic compounds and vegetable oils.

It may reduce the viscosity of surfactant-based formulations.

The right dosage of the solubiliser will vary according to what you are solubilising; start
with a 1:3 ratio (one part oil, three parts solubiliser). If the final formulation is cloudy, you
might need to add more solubiliser.

Vigorous stirring may produce some foam; mix it gently.

name: Aloe vera
inci: Aloe Barbadensis Leaf Extract or Aloe Barbadensis Leaf Juice
function: Emollient, humectant, oral care, skin conditioning
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Aloe vera, also called Aloe barbadensis, is a succulent plant that contains gel inside its
leaves. Aloe's extracts can be used in cosmetics and topical products.

This plant has been used for a long time, since the ancient Egyptians. It is used topically
for the treatment of burns, sunburns, inflammatory skin disorders and wounds.

Studies have shown that treatment with Aloe vera extracts can promote skin repair. This
property may be partially due to its content of acemannan, a compound that stimulates
cells that take part in the cicatrization process.

Furthermore, aloe is able to increase the content of antioxidant enzymes (glutathione
peroxidase and superoxide dismutase) in cells while also promoting collagen synthesis
and diminishing the damage caused by free radicals. Moreover, aloe has antibacterial and
antifungal action.

Aloe's high polysaccharide content makes it an effective ingredient for improving skin
hydration. It alleviates sunburn, helping the skin to heal faster by repairing the connective
tissue. It also has soothing properties that make it a good ingredient for rejuvenating
products. It can be used in products directed to after-sun care, and for acne-prone, itchy
and sensitive skin.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use the powdered version which you can dissolve before adding it to water-containing
products such as toners, emulsions, shower gels, eye gels or even hair rinses. The gel is
often thickened up by the use of gums such as xanthan, and has added water.

Usually, aloe extracts are water based. You can find aqueous extracts, glycerites and extracts
made with propanediol (a natural humectant).

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Add it in the cool down phase or to cold process emulsions.

name: Beetroot glycerite
inci: Glycerin (and) Aqua (and) Beta Vulgaris Root Extract
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Beetroot is known for its deep and powerful purplish-red pigments and is considered a
source of bioactive antioxidants. It is used for its colour giving compounds. Betalains,
water-soluble pigments, are the major purplish-red pigment in the red beetroot.

Beetroot contains compounds such as betalains and other pigments, with antioxidant
properties that prevent the adverse effects of oxidative stress and the effects of free
radicals. It also exhibits antibacterial and antiviral properties.

Freshly grated beetroot, added to glycerine, yields a beautiful pink that can also be used
as a colourant in water-containing products.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in toners, facial mists, facial cleansers, shampoos, body cleansers and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Add it in the cool down phase or to cold process emulsions. These pigments are hard to
stabilise in terms of colour, as they are sensitive to heat, light, oxygen, and pH variations.
You will possibly see your formulations lose their colour over time.

name: Calendula petals and macerated oil
function: Petals: Skin conditioning Extract: Fragrance, skin conditioning
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Ancient Egyptians and Romans used calendula for cosmetic and medicinal purposes.
At first, calendula was used as a food colouring in cheese if saffron was not available.

Some compounds present in calendula petals are terpenoids, flavonoids, coumarins,
quinones, saponins, mucilage, volatile oils, carotenoids (mainly lutein and zeaxanthin),
and amino acids.

Calendula oil is made by infusing the flowers in a base oil until it has extracted the
oil-soluble components of the petals. Bases typically used for calendula oil are olive oil,
sunflower oil or sweet almond oil.

Herbalists value calendula as a plant that helps with skin recovery. It has been widely
used as a remedy since ancient times. Calendula stimulates the regeneration of skin
cells and exerts a calming and relaxing effect, especially on irritated and inflamed skin.
It is excellent for sensitive skin. Calendula also presents anti-inflammatory, antiseptic,
antioxidant, antibacterial, and analgesic effects. Use it in products designed for minor skin
issues, cuts and wounds, inflamed and irritated skin. It is good for sunburn, acne, and even
rashes.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use calendula in your cosmetics in the form of a macerated oil, infusion, tincture,
CO2 extract, or powder.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Also known as pot marigold, calendula should not be confused with other types of plants
more commonly known as marigold, such as those in the genus Tagetes.

Although very rare, allergic reactions can occur in a small percentage of the population.
Therefore, it is advised that anyone allergic to the Asteraceae (daisy) family should use it
with caution. Always do a patch test with new herbs when you are experimenting with them.

name: Carrot macerated oil
inci: Name Of The Carrier Oil (and) Daucus Carota Sativa Root Extract
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Carrot oil is a macerated oil. The carrot's roots are infused in a carrier oil – often sesame
oil, sunflower oil or olive oil. The resulting macerated oil has a bright orange colour and is
sometimes used as a yellow food colouring.

This oil helps improve the skin repair process by assisting in the formation of scar tissue.
It also soothes itchy and inflamed skin.

The oil contains a high percentage of beta-carotene, which is an excellent antioxidant. For
that reason, carrot macerated oil is often used in anti-ageing skincare products. It is said
to be particularly useful for the (ageing) neck due to its claimed reputation for delaying the
ageing process.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Lip balms, haircare, nail care, anhydrous creams, balms, butters, scrubs, and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It has a strong orange colour. Do not confuse the macerated oil with the carrot seed
essential oil.

                            ACTIVE BOTANICALS:

name: Chamomile
inci: Anthemis Nobilis Flower Powder or Chamomilla Recutita Flower
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Roman chamomile (Anthemis nobilis) is traditionally considered to be an antiseptic,
antibiotic, bactericidal, and fungicidal plant. The main phenolic compounds found in
Roman chamomile herbal material are flavonoids, phenolic acids and their derivatives.

German chamomile (Chamomilla recutita) extracts have anti-inflammatory properties
and are used for many different skin conditions. Chamazulene, alpha-bisabolol and
apigenin are the main active compounds found in this plant, all of them presenting anti-
inflammatory properties. German chamomile has a higher chamazulene content than
Roman chamomile. However, this substance is only found in the essential oil because it is
produced during the distillation process from another compound, called matricin.

Chamomile's mucilage content lends this plant some soothing properties. It has been
used for centuries, providing anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, antibacterial, and mild
astringent effects. External applications of its extracts are recommended for their
emollient and anti-inflammatory action on sensitive skin and are widely applied in
cosmetic formulations.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use chamomile in your cosmetics in the form of essential oil, as a macerated oil, infusion,
glycerite, tincture, or even as a CO2 extract. Add it to shampoos, creams and balms,
massage oils or even facial steams.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Although very rare, allergic reactions can occur in a small percentage of the population.
Therefore, it is advised that anyone allergic to the Asteraceae (daisy) family should use it
with caution. Always do a patch test with new herbs when you are experimenting with them.

name: Comfrey
inci: Symphytum Officinale Leaf Extract or Symphytum Officinale Root Extract
function: Leaf: Skin conditioning Root: Anti-seborrheic, skin conditioning, soothing
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Comfrey’s (Symphytum officinale) main pharmacological activity is to stimulate tissue
regeneration. Its main active ingredients are allantoin and rosmarinic acid. It also contains
chlorogenic acid, caffeic acid as well as various vitamins and minerals.

The parts of comfrey that are often used are the roots and the leaves. Ancient Greeks
used comfrey to stop bleeding and also to treat wounds and help with broken bones.
This plant also has anti-inflammatory, analgesic, anti-edematous and astringent effects.
Its high carbohydrate content is said to help with skin rejuvenation.

Allantoin is considered responsible for this plant's regenerative properties. It also acts as a
moisturising and keratolytic agent, providing anti-irritant and protective effects on the skin.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in glycerite form or as a tincture. You can also try it as an infusion or as powder.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Comfrey contains compounds called pyrrolizidine alkaloids, which can be toxic when
ingested. Consider how you apply comfrey in your formulations, as you may not want to
incorporate it into lip balms, for instance. Comfrey should not be applied to broken skin for
this reason.

name: Cucumber glycerite
inci: Glycerin (and) Aqua (and) Cucumis Sativus Fruit Extract
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Cucumber, or Cucumis sativus, is widely used for various skin problems, frequently for
soothing irritated skin, whether caused by the sun, or the effects of cutaneous eruptions.It
promotes refreshing, cooling, soothing, emollient, and anti-itching effects to irritated skin.

The aqueous extract of cucumber is used in cosmetics as a skin conditioning, emollient,
refreshing and toning agent. It contains glycosides, steroids, flavonoids, carbohydrates,
terpenoids, and tannins. It also exerts antioxidant activity. The lutein content in cucumber
may help with pigmentation issues. As cucumber is astringent, it is a good choice for oily
skin and scalp.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Toners, facial mists, facial cleansers, gels, shampoos, body cleansers, and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects are known.

name: Green tea glycerite
inci: Glycerin (and) Aqua (and) Camellia Sinensis Leaf Extract
function: Antimicrobial, antioxidant, astringent, fragrance, emollient, humectant, oral care, skin conditioning, skin protecting, tonic
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Green tea glycerite is known to have anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, antioxidant, and anti-
ageing properties. It contains polyphenols and catechin derivatives, the main components
of the plant's leaves. These compounds are known to be remarkable antioxidants, acting
against lipid peroxidation and preventing the photo-ageing process. Thanks to these
properties, green tea extract is found in many anti-ageing products.

Besides catechins, green tea contains various other compounds, such as methylxanthines,
like caffeine and theophylline. It also has proteins, amino acids, carbohydrates, and lipids
such as linoleic and linolenic acids. Vitamins B, C and E, pigments such as chlorophyll and
carotenoids, volatile compounds and minerals are also present.

Studies conducted with cosmetics containing green tea extracts have shown significant
results on skin moisturising effects, on the improvement of the skin's texture and
appearance, as well as antimicrobial activity against skin pathogens.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Toners, facial mists, facial cleansers, shampoos, body cleansers, and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects are known.

name: Horsetail glycerite
inci: Glycerin (and) Aqua (and) Equisetum Arvense Extract or
function: Astringent, emollient, skin conditioning, soothing, tonic
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Horsetail (Equisetum arvense) extract presents anti-oxidative, antimicrobial, anti-
inflammatory and vasorelaxant properties.

Constituents in horsetail include polyphenolic derivatives (flavonoids, styrylpyrones, and
phenolic acids), alkaloids (equisetin, nicotine, palustrine, and palustrinine), phytosterols
(campesterol), minerals (silica, calcium, magnesium, selenium, iron, potassium, zinc, etc.),
vitamins (C, E, K, B1, B2, B6), and tannins (bitter principle).

No other herb in the entire plant kingdom is as rich in silicic acids and silicates as
horsetail. Silicic acid modulates the activity of enzymes that produce collagen. Collagen is
a structural protein that gives the skin mechanical strength and resiliency. It is needed by
your skin for the normal regeneration of healthy skin tissues.

Although there is little scientific evidence of horsetail's properties, it has been used to
improve skin, hair, and nails' strength, tone, and texture. Traditionally, it is said to provide
astringent, tonic, revitalising, soothing and antioxidant properties.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Toners, facial mists, facial cleansers, shampoos, body cleansers, and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects are known.

name: Irish moss
inci: Chondrus Crispus Powder or Chondrus Crispus Extract or Carrageenan
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Irish moss (Chondrus crispus) is a dried seaweed that is also called carrageen moss.

Carrageenans, the main components of Irish moss, are linear, water-soluble, anionic
polymers. They form highly viscous aqueous solutions that are used as thickeners and
stabilising agents. Also, they are said to have anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antiviral
activity. They can help maintain the health and smoothness of the skin.
