There are different types of carrageenan, mainly kappa, iota and lambda, which differ in
their degree of sulphation. Kappa and iota carrageenans form thermo-reversible gels.
Typically, carrageenans are sold as stabilised salts of sodium, potassium, or calcium.

Kappa carrageenan forms rigid and brittle gels in the presence of potassium ions. It can
present syneresis, an undesired phenomenon in which the gel expels part of the liquid.
It works in synergy with xanthan gum, which helps to create gels that are more elastic
and cohesive.

Iota carrageenan forms elastic and transparent gels in the presence of calcium ions.
It does not present syneresis and is the most interesting type for cosmetic use.

Lambda carrageenan is not a gelling agent, but forms viscous solutions in water.

Carrageenans also provide an emollient action on nails and hairs, thanks to the specific
way they bind to keratin fibres.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in gels, gel masks, and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Carrageenan is a vegan alternative to gelatin. At high temperatures and low pH, carrageenans
can lose their functionality. In skincare, we use carrageenan as a thickener (gum).

There are some concerns regarding the safety of carrageenan. However, this comes
from studies where it is used in its degraded form or injected subcutaneously to induce
inflammation. The topical use of cosmetic grade carrageenan is considered safe and should
not cause any concern.

name: Kelp/seaweed powder
inci: There are different INCI names depending on the seaweed species. Some
function: Laminaria digitata: Skin conditioning Laminaria japonica: Skin conditioning Lessonia nigrescens: Binding, viscosity controlling Undaria pinnatifida: Absorbent, binding, viscosity controlling Ascophyllum nodosum: Skin conditioning
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
There are various species of seaweed used in cosmetics, which can be found at suppliers
as kelp or seaweed powder.

There is evidence that brown algae contribute the most to cosmetic products. Although
from different species, generally, these algae are rich in vitamins from the B complex,
vitamin E, amino acids, fatty acids, polysaccharides, and minerals like calcium, potassium,
magnesium, iodine, and iron. They can present antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial,
emollient, moisturising, and energising activity, and they notably stimulate circulation, being
used in anti-cellulite products.

Laminaria species are considered promising ingredients to improve the appearance of
uneven skin colour due to influences on the melanogenesis process. Also, these seaweeds
have the potential to reduce excessive oil production and help to relieve skin irritation.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Powdered algae can be used in body and face masks, scrubs and cleansing formulations.
You can also use the powder to infuse in oil or glycerine.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Most algae present a subtle or strong fish-like aroma, which can be hard to overcome with
other fragrances. No adverse effects are known.

name: Lady's mantle
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Lady’s mantle is also called bear’s foot or lion’s foot. The leaves and roots are the parts
used for making extracts.

This plant presents astringent, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory effects. It contains
tannins (mainly composed of gallic and ellagic acid) and flavonoids, the most abundant
being quercetin.

In skincare, we can use this plant for chapped skin, especially for hands and feet. As it is
astringent, you can also use it to improve the appearance of enlarged pores. Its tannin's
content can help dry wounds and reduce inflammation, making lady’s mantle useful in
the care of acne-prone skin.

Lady's mantle powder can be used in body and face masks, scrubs and cleansing
formulations. You can always use the powder to infuse in oil or glycerine.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in oil infusions, facial steams, infusions, scrubs, and soaps.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects known.

name: Marshmallow root
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Althaea officinalis is a plant commonly known as marshmallow. Its polysaccharides and
flavonoids are responsible for its therapeutic benefits.

This plant presents skin repair and emollient properties. It also provides analgesic, anti-
inflammatory, antioxidant, and antibacterial effects. The polysaccharides in this plant also
help to stimulate tissue regeneration.

Marshmallow roots have water-soluble polysaccharides such as galacturorhamnans,
arabinans, glucans and arabinogalactans. They also contain phenolic acids, tannins,
flavone glycosides, coumarin, pectin and other compounds.

Marshmallow aqueous extracts have been used traditionally for treating irritated mucous
membranes and as a soothing and anti-itching emollient.

This plant is a very useful medicinal herb, as its soothing properties make it very effective
in treating inflammation and irritation of the skin. The whole plant, but especially the root,
is high in mucilage and highly emollient. Mucilage will create a gel-like substance that is
calming, which is particularly useful to inflamed areas of the skin.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Toners, facial mists, facial cleansers, shampoos, body cleansers and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects known.

name: Monoi de tahiti
inci: Cocos Nucifera Oil (and) Gardenia Taitensis Flower Extract
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
If you ever want to incorporate a beautiful floral oil into your formulations, you should try
Monoi de Tahiti. Made by macerating Tahitian gardenia (tiare) flower buds in coconut
oil for 15 days, changing the flowers every 2 to 3 days, this is one of the most fragrant
macerated oils available. The scent is simply incredible!

As we saw, coconut oil is rich in saturated fatty acids and becomes liquid over 24 °C (75 °F).
Monoi de Tahiti oil is the same and has the same rich moisturising properties – especially
for dry, flaky skin, or as an after-sun moisturiser. It also has uses as a bath oil and to
condition dry hair. Polynesian women are known to apply this luxurious, heavenly-scented
oil to their skin and hair.

Tahitian monoi oil has been produced commercially since 1942 and has the French
Government “Appellation d’origine” (guarantee of origin).

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use the oil in lip care, haircare, body care such as anhydrous creams, balms, butters,
scrubs, and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects known.

name: Mullein (verbascum)
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Plants from the Verbascus genus have been used for centuries in folk medicine due to
their wide range of biological activities. The antimicrobial and antioxidant effects of these
plants are described in scientific literature.

Verbascum thapsus is one of the most common species from this genus, and also has
significant skin repair, pain relief, and anti-inflammatory properties.

Some constituents of Verbascum plants are polysaccharides, iridoid glycosides,
flavonoids, saponins, and volatile oils. Verbascoside is one of the main phenolic
compounds found in this plant, presenting anaesthetic and analgesic effects.

Although there is little scientific data regarding Verbascum oil macerates, there are some
registers in the literature about mullein oil. It is produced by macerating its flowers in olive
oil and is used for frostbite, bruises, and dry skin conditions.

Mullein’s leaves, roots, and flowers have astringent properties and provide emollience.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use the macerated oil in lip, hair, and body care. It can be used in products such as
anhydrous creams, balms, butters, scrubs, and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Some research suggests that mullein leaf may cause skin irritation. Some compounds
found in mullein seeds are also thought to be unsuitable for human use or consumption.
Always undertake a patch test when working with new herbs.

name: Nettle
inci: Urtica Dioica Leaf Powder or Urtica Dioica Extract or Urtica Dioica Leaf Extract
function: Leaf powder: Abrasive Plant extract: Anti-seborrheic, astringent, hair conditioning, skin conditioning, soothing, tonic Leaf extract: Skin conditioning
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Stinging nettle has a long history of use in cosmetics. The leaves are mainly chosen,
although the whole plant is suitable for this purpose.

It is a good source of flavonoids, phenylpropanoids, and caffeic acid analogues. It is used
for the treatment of sensitive skin and has antioxidant activity.

Nettle is rich in carotenoids, vitamins B2, C, E, and mineral elements such as potassium,
calcium, magnesium, iron, zinc, and others. Its extracts exhibit antioxidant activity related
to its phenolic compounds. Nettle extracts have noticeable antimicrobial activity against
Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Add nettle to skincare products, such as toners and emulsions directed to acne-prone
or sensitive skin. You can also use it for haircare in products such as shampoo or hair
conditioners.

You can use nettle powder in dry formulations such as masks and cleansing powders.
Likewise, you can use it in scrubs or to make extracts in oil or glycerine.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects known.

name: Oat
inci: Avena Sativa Meal Extract or Avena Sativa Kernel Extract or Colloidal Oatmeal
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Oat, Avena sativa, has been used for centuries to soothe and protect dry, itchy, inflamed
skin. It possesses antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and anti-itching properties.

There are different grades of oats available on the market. They all generally increase
viscosity, enhance emulsion stability and leave a smooth skin feel. In addition to its colloid
providing a soothing effect on the skin, oats also contain vegetable protein.

Oatmeal (finely ground oats) possesses different types of phenols, with avenanthramides
as the most important. Phenolic compounds in oatmeal exert antioxidant and anti-
inflammatory activity. Avenanthramides are said to be responsible for the potent anti-
inflammatory and anti-irritant effects of oats.

Oatmeal also works as a moisturising ingredient. It has a high polysaccharide content
that forms a protective film over the skin, delaying water loss. It also helps to repair and
maintain the epidermal barrier.

Regarding polysaccharides, oat beta-glucan has been claimed to help fight the signs of
ageing, activate collagen synthesis, and strengthen hair fibres. A combination of beta-
glucan and hydrolysed oat protein can be used to moisturise and soothe irritated skin.

Oatmeal saponins help to solubilise dirt, oil and sebaceous secretions and are responsible
for oatmeal’s cleansing property.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Toner, facial mists, facial cleanser, shampoos, body cleansers, and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects known.

name: Orris root
inci: Iris Florentina Root Extract or Iris Germanica Root Extract or
function: Iris florentina: Fragrance, tonic Iris germanica: Skin conditioning Iris pallida: Fragrance, tonic
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Iris germanica, Iris pallida, and Iris florentina roots are used to produce the orris root
(rhizoma iridis) powder. Many cultures and countries have used it over the centuries, and
the flower was the symbol of the French monarchy.

This ingredient was used in tooth powders and is said to help teething babies.

Orris roots have a violet flower aroma and are used primarily as a fixative in perfumes to
enhance other aromas.

The main chemical components of Iris species are xanthones, isoflavones, quinones,
flavones, terpenes, sterols, ceramides, and phenolic compounds. These constituents have
multiple biological activities.

In skincare, orris root can help with the elasticity of the skin. It is refreshing and could
work well in masks and scrubs.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in powder form or make an infusion. Try to make your own perfume by soaking orris
root in alcohol or vodka for approx. 2 weeks.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
There are some reported cases of allergy to orris extracts, so always do a patch test with
new herbs when you are experimenting with them.

name: Rose petals
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Historically, rose petals have been used mainly for their astringent, antioxidant and
soothing properties.

Rose petals can vary in chemical composition and bioactivity, depending on the species
in question. They can contain various biologically active compounds including phenolic
acids, such as gallic acid, and flavonoids, such as rutin, quercitrin, myricetin, quercetin
and kaempferol. Syringic acid and anthocyanins may be present and contribute to rose’s
antioxidant properties.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use dried rose petals for infusions, or grind them and use them in scrubs, masks, and
soaps. You can also add the petals to bath melts, bath bombs and bath salts.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects known.

name: Sea buckthorn macerated oil
inci: Name Of The Carrier Oil (and) Hippophae Rhamnoides Fruit Extract
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
The spiny shrubs grow on seaside dunes, which have given rise to the common name.
In Western Europe, sea buckthorn thrives in the seashores, where salt spray deters other
plants in competition. This plant grows well in dry semidesert regions in Asia, where other
plants struggle to survive.

Sea buckthorn oil extract is produced by macerating the berries in a base oil, typically
olive oil. The maceration takes on a deep orangey-red colour. Sea buckthorn oil has a
high essential fatty acid content and also contains many other compounds, including
antioxidants.

Sea buckthorn oil can be extracted from either the seed or the fruit's pulp, both of which
contain different anti-ageing compounds. It is readily absorbed and has a high content
of essential fatty acids, carotenes, tocopherols and phytosterols, which help to repair
the skin's lipid barrier and keep the skin healthy.

The oil is an ideal choice for any anti-ageing blend. It also helps in dry skin conditions.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use the oil in lip care, haircare, body care such as anhydrous creams, balms, butters,
scrubs, and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Sea buckthorn macerate and CO2 extract present a strong orange colour, so keep this in
mind when formulating with these ingredients.

name: Spirulina
inci: Spirulina Maxima Powder or Spirulina Platensis Powder
function: Spirulina maxima: Antioxidant, viscosity controlling Spirulina platensis: Skin protecting
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Spirulina is a type of photosynthetic cyanobacteria that is among the most popularly
cultivated microalgae. It includes various species of primitive unicellular blue-green algae,
such as Arthrospira platensis and Arthrospira maxima. The genus Arthrospira was formerly
classified as Spirulina, and this name is still used in their INCI.

Spirulina contains a wide variety of nutrients, including proteins, polyunsaturated fatty
acids, polysaccharides, carotenoids, vitamins, and minerals such as calcium, magnesium,
phosphorus, potassium, sodium, and zinc.

Spirulina extract has hydrating properties, helping reinforce the skin barrier and reducing
transepidermal water loss.

Spirulina's antioxidant properties help to prevent premature skin ageing. Spirulina has also
been used to reduce hyperpigmentation due to its component called C-phycocyanin, which
has shown anti-melanogenic activity in vitro.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in masks, scrubs, and soaps.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Spirulina can present a subtle or strong fish-like aroma, which can be difficult to overcome
with other fragrances. No adverse effects are known.

name: St. john's wort macerated oil
inci: Name Of Carrier Oil (and) Hypericum Perforatum Extract
function: Antimicrobial, astringent, fragrance, skin conditioning, skin protecting, soothing, tonic
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
St. John’s Wort oil is a maceration of the buds and flowers of this summer-flowering herb
into a carrier oil, traditionally olive oil.

Hypericum perforatum is widely known in traditional medicine for its skin repair effects
and its use in the treatments of damaged skin and burns. Among its phytochemical
constituents are hypericin (which gives a deep red colour to the oil), pseudohypericin,
hyperforin, adhyperforin, and flavonoids such as quercetin, quercitrin, hyperoside, rutin,
kaempferol, biapigenin, and amentoflavone, as well as xanthones. A study found that
almond oil was able to extract higher amounts of hypericin, while fractionated coconut oil
(medium-chain triglycerides, or MCT) extracted higher yields of flavonoids, like quercetin
and kaempferol.

In skincare, we use this macerate for its soothing properties. It is also said to be anti-
inflammatory and astringent. With up to 40% hyperforin, the supercritical CO2 extract can
be used in products for acne-prone and sensitive skin.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in products for after-sun skincare and sensitive skin. Use the oil in lip care, haircare,
body care such as anhydrous creams, balms, butters, scrubs, and emulsions.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It has a red colour when macerated. St John’s Wort contains hypericin, which can induce
photosensitization in prone subjects. CO2 extraction of the plant material allows the
separation of hyperforin from hypericin.

name: Activated charcoal
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Activated charcoal is a very fine powder of black colour that does not actually belong to
the clay class. It can be beneficial for acne-prone and oily skin.

Although its function is officially described as absorbent – which would mean the
molecules are drawn into its particles, like in a sponge, it is, in fact, an adsorbent material.
This means that other molecules adhere to the activated charcoal's surface, and it is able
to remove these impurities, helping to clean the skin.

CHARACTERISTICS
Activated charcoal can be tricky to work with but presents benefits for those with acne-
prone or inflamed skin.

Using too much in a formula can result in tiny little specks getting stuck in the skin pores,
making rinsing off quite difficult. It can be used along with other clays, depending on what
you wish your formula to do.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in facial masks, facial polishes, body skincare formulations, body masks, cleansing
balms, and deodorants.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Keep in mind that a small amount gives a strong black colour to formulations.

Charcoal is not easy to work with. Make sure you wear a mask when formulating with
charcoal, as it is a fine powder that can be easily inhaled.

Avoid humidity and store it under dry conditions.

name: Bentonite
function: Absorbent, bulking, emulsion stabilising, viscosity controlling
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
This natural clay consists primarily of montmorillonite, a member of the smectite group of
clays. It is formed by the devitrification of volcanic ash or tuff. Bentonite is mainly sourced
from China, USA, and India and was originally named for the smectite clay found near
Fort Benton, Montana. After extraction, it is dried in the sun, retaining its mineral salts and
beneficial properties.

CHARACTERISTICS
This clay presents great water-absorbing and thickening properties. It is used in skin
cleansing and is especially good for oily or combination skin types. It is less drying than
illite clay.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Bentonite has a variety of uses in cosmetics, including facial masks and polishes, body
skincare formulations, haircare products, mineral make-ups, soaps, and cleansing balms.

Use it in products for cleansing, refreshing dull or clogged skin and soothing irritated skin.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It can inactivate cationic preservatives. Products containing water and clay are hard
to preserve.

name: Dead sea mud/sea silt
inci: Maris Limus Extract or Sea Silt
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
It is a unique, mineral-rich, brown, hypersaline mud mined from the Dead Sea shores and
extensively used since ancient times. Dead Sea mineral mud has been used for a long
time for beauty purposes and to alleviate dry skin conditions.

It presents antimicrobial properties and a gritty texture, making it a good ingredient for
scrubs, and it can also be used in facial masques. This mud is rich in minerals found at
the bottom of the Dead Sea and adds that extra luxurious touch to spa treatments

CHARACTERISTICS
Dead Sea mud is extremely high in various salts and contains high concentrations of
magnesium, sodium, phosphates, bromides, and other minerals. It is a sought-after
treatment in spas all over the world. It looks brown when you apply it in a facial or body
masque.

Scientific studies found that it exhibits antimicrobial activity against strains of skin
microorganisms such as E. coli, S. aureus, P. acnes and C. albicans.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in facial and body masks and scrubs.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Products containing water and clay are hard to preserve.

name: Green clay
function: Illite: Abrasive, absorbent, anticaking, bulking Montmorillonite: Absorbent, bulking, emulsion stabilising, light stabiliser, viscosity controlling
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
This ingredient is also known as French green clay, green illite clay, or sea clay. That is one
of the most common yet luxurious clays used in the global cosmetics industry.

Green clay can be composed of montmorillonite and illite, or only the first. It owes its
colours to iron oxides and decomposed plant matter. Always check when you buy green
clay that it is truly green or off-green in colour.

It contains up to nine mineral oxides, including magnesium, calcium, potassium, dolomite,
silica, manganese, phosphorous, silicon, copper, and selenium.

Green clay doesn't always come from France, as deposits are found all over the world.
Since the original green clays came from France, the name has stuck.

CHARACTERISTICS
It helps remove impurities from the skin and tighten it up, making it feel more toned.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in facial masks, facial polishes, body skincare formulations, body masks, cleansing
balms, and soaps.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Products containing water and clay are hard to preserve.

name: Kaolin
function: Abrasive, absorbent, anticaking, bulking, colourant, opacifying
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Otherwise known as China clay or ceramic clay, it is found in almost all powder-based
cosmetics and is one of the most common cosmetic clays used today.

The name comes from the Chinese Gaoling, a reference to a mountain in China that
provided an early source of this raw mineral.

CHARACTERISTICS
It provides gentle cleansing, is absorbent, and helps remove dirt and excess oil. It gives
a velvety feel to the skin. Also, it has high levels of silica, which can help with skin
rejuvenation.

Depending on the minerals present in kaolin clay, it can present a wide variety of colours,
from white to pink, orange, red, violet, yellow, green, and black.

It is well-tolerated by all skin types.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
It has a wide variety of uses in cosmetics, including facial masks, polishes and powders,
body skincare formulations, hygiene and haircare products, oral hygiene preparations,
mineral make-ups, cleansing balms, and soaps.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Products containing water and clay are hard to preserve.

name: Red clay
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Red clay is good at drawing oils and dirt from the skin and is suitable for oily skin. It does
not expand upon contact with water. It turns brick red when activated and can stain carpets,
towels and clothing, so be sure to place a warning on your product label for your customer.

CHARACTERISTICS
The red clay gets its colour primarily from high levels of iron oxide. It is mainly composed
of kaolin-type clay. However, it is less rich in minerals than other clays. It contains more
silicate and has ideal firming properties for mature and loose skin.

Red clay is able to reduce skin oiliness and increase firmness and elasticity. Pink clay is
actually a blend of white and red kaolin clay.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it for cleansing and exfoliation. Use it in facial masks and polishes, body skincare
formulations, body masks, and cleansing balms.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Products containing water and clay are hard to preserve.

name: Rhassoul
function: Abrasive, absorbent, bulking, emulsion stabilising, opacifying, viscosity controlling
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Rhassoul is also known as Moroccan clay. It has a reddish to brown colour and provides
a cleansing effect, absorbing excess sebum and dirt from the skin. The name rhassoul
derives from the Arabic rhassala, which means “to wash”. This clay is traditionally used in
skin and haircare products.

CHARACTERISTICS
This clay contains higher percentages of stevensite, silica, magnesium, potassium, and
calcium than other clays.

It provides gentle cleansing, is absorbent, and helps to remove dirt and excess oil. It is
well-liked in no-poo hair cleansers and is well-tolerated by all skin types, but it is especially
useful for oily and acne-prone skin.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
It has a wide variety of uses in cosmetics, including facial masks and polishes, body
skincare formulations, body masks, cleansing balms, and haircare products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Products containing water and clay are hard to preserve.

name: Almond meal
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Almond meal is made of soft powdery grains and provides a delicate exfoliation. It is
produced from ground blanched almonds. It is suitable for any skin type and commonly
used in body scrubs for gentle exfoliation. It is also delicate enough to be used daily.

In Ayurveda, it is mixed with other ingredients to make Ubtan. It is a tradition to use this
mixture to soften the bride's skin, so she can look radiant on her wedding day.

CHARACTERISTICS
It is suitable for products for all skin types. You can use polishes and scrubs with almond
meal daily, as they are gentle to the skin.

Use it as the sole exfoliant, or mix it with others. You can combine it with coarser
exfoliants such as sugar in body scrubs.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in facial polishes and body scrubs.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects are known.

name: Apricot kernel powder
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
It is made by grinding the apricot’s kernel. It can have many particle sizes, so make sure to
check this information with your supplier.

CHARACTERISTICS
Its particle size may not be suitable for facial skincare products. Usually, this is a
coarse exfoliator.

If you wish to use it in facial products, you will need to grind it into a powdery texture with
fine particles. This is because the shape of this exfoliant may cause micro-tears on
the skin.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in body, hand, and foot scrubs.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Avoid it in facial skincare products.

name: Adzuki beans powder
inci: Vigna Angularis Seed Powder or Phaseolus Angularis Seed Powder
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
This ingredient is a soft powder made from finely milled adzuki beans, an annual climbing
plant cultivated throughout Asia since the year 1000.

You can also do this yourself, using dried adzuki beans and grinding them in a coffee
grinder.

The adzuki bean is rich in both saponins and minerals. Its proanthocyanidins content give
this red bean potent antioxidant benefits.

CHARACTERISTICS
This exfoliant works for both facial and body exfoliation. It can be used on its own or
blended with other scrub particles.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in facial, body, hand, and foot scrubs.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects are known.

name: Bamboo powder
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Bamboo powder is an exfoliant that can have various sizes, but is usually sold as a very
fine powder with small particles.

It is a safe and gentle ingredient that effectively exfoliates the outer layer of the skin.

This ingredient is a white powder extracted from the exudate present in the medulla of
bamboo stems, also known as tabashir, which has a high silica content.

CHARACTERISTICS
Bamboo is rich in silica, which makes it useful for its remineralising properties. That is
why it is a good choice for anti-ageing and anti-acne products.

It is effective when used on its own or blended with other exfoliants.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in facial polishes, body, hand, and foot scrubs.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects are known.

name: Jojoba beads
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Jojoba beads are made from fully hydrogenated jojoba wax, shaped in uniform spheres.
They are available as a biodegradable alternative to synthetic polymer microbeads, which
cause environmental concerns and are already banned in several countries.

CHARACTERISTICS
Jojoba beads have a uniform spherical shape and are suitable for body scrubs and facial
polishes. Their form will not irritate the skin or cause microtears. They are odourless and
white in general, but you can also get them in various colours. They are also biodegradable
and safe for the environment.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in facial polishes, body, hand, and foot scrubs.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
We find the coloured jojoba beads can alter the scent of the final product, so keep this in
mind when formulating with them.

name: Mineral salts
inci: Sodium Chloride or Sea Salt or Maris Sal
function: Bulking, fragrance, oral care, viscosity controlling
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Quality salts such as Himalayan, Dead Sea and Cornish Sea salt contain skin-soothing
minerals. These salts are excellent bases for body scrubs. However, they can irritate
sensitive or damaged skin.

Salt is not recommended for use in facial polish, as it can cause microtears on the skin.

CHARACTERISTICS
Use it with carrier oils or butters to create anhydrous scrubs. Avoid using salt in O/W
emulsions as some emulsifiers are sensitive to electrolytes, which could cause the
separation of phases.

Considering that salt is also a humectant (it attracts water to itself), you may find that
it can melt over time or in hot climates, so keep on experimenting to find a formula that
works for you.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in body, hand, and foot scrubs.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It is not recommended for use in facial polish.

Avoid adding it to O/W emulsions.

name: Oatmeal
inci: Avena Sativa Kernel Meal or Avena Sativa Kernel Flour or Colloidal Oatmeal
function: Avena sativa kernel meal: Abrasive, absorbent, bulking Avena sativa kernel flour: Abrasive, absorbent, bulking, viscosity controlling Colloidal oatmeal: Abrasive, absorbent, bulking, skin protecting
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Oatmeal is a skin-soothing exfoliating ingredient rich in silica. Avenanthramides are
substances responsible for the potent anti-inflammatory and anti-irritant effects of oats.

CHARACTERISTICS
Oatmeal has a popular reputation for alleviating the symptoms of inflammatory skin
conditions, helping to restore the cutaneous barrier and reduce transepidermal water loss.
It presents soothing properties, which makes it a good choice for sensitive skin.

Use the medium oatmeal for the body and the fine oatmeal for the face. You can also buy
raw oat groats and powder your own.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in facial polishes, body, hand, and foot scrubs.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects are known.

name: Pumice
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Pumice is a fine powder made from volcanic rock consisting primarily of complex silicates
of aluminium and alkali metals. It can be found in many grades, so check this information
with your supplier to see the best choice for you.

CHARACTERISTICS
It is great to use on tough body areas such as calloused feet, knees, and elbows. It is
effective when used on its own or blended with other scrub particles.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in body scrubs, hand, and foot polish.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It is not recommended for facial polishes.

name: Rapadura sugar
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Rapadura is unrefined whole cane sugar made from evaporated cane juice. As it is not
just sucrose separated from the molasses, it is rich in minerals and alpha-hydroxy acids
(which are chemical exfoliators). It promotes rejuvenation of the top layers of your skin.

CHARACTERISTICS
It is a gentle exfoliating ingredient used in body and facial polishes. It has a lovely,
caramel-like aroma, which may affect the final product. Keep this in mind when
formulating, but also you can plan around this. Pair it with vanilla or citrus essential oils,
which will work well with the natural scent of rapadura.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in facial polishes, body, hand, and foot scrubs.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
No adverse effects are known.

name: Walnut shell powder
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
This exfoliant is made by grinding the shell of the walnut. There are different grades, from
coarse to fine powders, but because of the uneven and rough shape of the particles, it is
not recommended for facial skincare products.

CHARACTERISTICS
It is good to use on tough body areas such as calloused feet, knees, and elbows. It is
effective on its own or blended with other scrub particles. You can add it to anhydrous
body scrubs, but this exfoliant can work well in emulsion bases as well.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in body, hand, and foot scrubs.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It is not recommended for facial polishes.

                  AROMACEUTICALS
Essential oils are volatile compounds characterised by a strong odour. They have been
used for centuries for therapeutical and cosmetic purposes. Essential oils are secondary
metabolites produced by plants and can occur in all plant organs.

Essential oils present a wide range of properties. For example, they can provide
antimicrobial, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory action or even help reduce local pain.

The biological activities presented by essential oils are important in cosmetology.
They can help alleviate many skin conditions, protect the skin against oxidative damage,
and slow down the ageing processes.

Essential oils are obtained from raw plant material. They can be extracted by steam
distillation or mechanical processes, such as cold-pressing the rind of citrus fruits.
The essential oils are soluble in lipids and organic solvents.

Aromatic plants can also undergo extraction processes with organic solvents. In this case,
they produce concretes, absolutes, or resinoids. They can also be extracted with liquid
carbon dioxide, producing CO2 extracts.

Components in essential oils can vary from extraction method or cultivar. We suggest that
you always check the constituents with your supplier.

Some essential oils present components known as sensitisers. We recommend that you
consult our Essential Oil Dermal Limits Guide to learn more about dermal limits, IFRA,
and regulations.

name: Benzoin resin oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Benzoin is an amber-coloured resin that has been valued for millennia, especially in the
Middle East and Asia. The benzoin resin has antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and skin-
repairing properties.

CHARACTERISTICS
Benzoin is a good choice for chapped, irritated and inflamed skin, as it presents antiseptic
and astringent properties. It has a sweet, vanilla-like fragrance, which makes it a great
addition to chocolatey skincare products. It is also a base note that can be used as
a fixative for other fragrances, imparting depth to the aromatic blend.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
It can be used in soothing products aimed at dry, irritated, and acne-prone skin. It can
be blended with jojoba for products aiming at acne-prone skin, or with calendula to soothe
skin irritations.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Benzoin oil has some components that may cause skin sensitisation. Check the Dermal
Limits Guide to learn more about this subject. Never use essential oils undiluted.

name: Bergamot essential oil
function: Fragrance, perfuming Fragrance family                         Citrus, fruity
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Bergamot is a wonderfully fragrant oil, which can be recognised as the fragrance of Earl
Grey tea. Its aroma is citrusy with a slightly fruity undertone. Named after the Italian town
of Bergamo, the oil is mainly produced in southern Italy or on the nearby island of Sicily.

CHARACTERISTICS
This oil possesses antimicrobial and analgesic properties. It can be blended with other
citrus oils and it is a good choice for oily skin.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in soothing products, emulsions, facial and body skincare, and haircare.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Never use essential oils undiluted. Please exercise caution when using, as this oil is
phototoxic. An antioxidant should be used when formulating with bergamot oil, as it can
oxidise due to its limonene content.

It is possible to buy rectified bergamot essential oil, which is furanocoumarin free (FCF).
That means it has its bergapten content removed, resulting in an oil without the potential
phototoxicity risk.

name: Carrot seed essential oil
function: Fragrance, skin conditioning, emollient Fragrance family                         Earthy, animalic
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Carrot seed oil is a good choice for all skincare products, especially facial products, as it
tones mature and dry skin and works to prevent wrinkles. Carrot seeds have a long history
of use in Europe and Asia and are renowned for their anti-inflammatory properties, along
with some antifungal activity.

CHARACTERISTICS
Carrot seed oil-based emulsions have been demonstrated to possess antioxidant
properties in vivo, which could reinforce its use on mature skin.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in face, body, and haircare products. Mix it with lemon essential oil to help reduce the
appearance of age spots.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It has a very strong aroma that some can find unpleasant. Never use essential oils
undiluted.

name: Chamomile essential oil
function: Fragrance, skin conditioning Fragrance family                       Herbaceous, green
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
German chamomile (Chamomilla recutita syn. Matricaria recutita syn. Matricaria
chamomilla) is also known as blue chamomile or Hungarian chamomile. The main
components of its essential oil are sesquiterpene derivatives such as alpha-bisabolol
and its oxides, and chamazulene. This oil possesses soothing properties and is good for
sensitive and problem skin.

CHARACTERISTICS
Studies suggest that alpha-bisabolol and chamazulene provide anti-inflammatory
properties. Chamazulene also presents anti-allergy effects. German chamomile essential
oil can reduce itching and allergies, and helps alleviate dry skin conditions.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
It can be blended with lavender for soothing products and balanced with sweet orange.
Usually, chamomile blends well with benzoin, bergamot, citrus oils, clary sage, frankincense,
geranium, jasmine, lavender, neroli, patchouli, rose, rosemary, tea tree, and ylang-ylang.

Use it in soothing products, emulsions, facial and body skincare, and haircare.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It has a strong aroma that some can find unpleasant. Never use essential oils undiluted.

Chamazulene is prone to oxidation, so always remember to store your chamomile essential
oil in dark, airtight containers protected from heat.

Although very rare, allergic reactions can occur in a small percentage of the population.
Therefore, it is advised that anyone allergic to the Asteraceae family, which includes both
species of chamomile, should use it with caution. Always do a patch test with new oils
when experimenting with them.

name: Clary sage essential oil
function: Fragrance, tonic Fragrance family                          Herbaceous, floral
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Clary sage essential oil has a sweet herbaceous aroma and is a good choice for products
for both dry and oily, acne-prone skin, as it helps to balance sebum production.

CHARACTERISTICS
This essential oil has antibacterial, antifungal, and antioxidant properties. In vitro tests
have shown that it also has the ability to reduce the appearance of hyperpigmentation.

The main components of clary sage essential oil are linalyl acetate, linalool, and
germacrene D. It also contains sclareol in small amounts.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in facial products for dry, oily, and acne-prone skin. It can also be used in deodorants.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Never use essential oils undiluted.

name: Frankincense essential oil
inci: Boswellia Carterii Gum Oil or Boswellia Serrata Oil, or Boswellia Sacra Resin Oil
function: Fragrance (Boswellia Carterii Gum Oil) Fragrance, skin conditioning (Boswellia Serrata Oil) Fragrance, perfuming, skin conditioning, emollient (Boswellia Sacra Resin Oil) Fragrance family                         Resinous
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Frankincense, also known as olibanum, is the common name given to the aromatic resin
produced by a group of trees belonging to the genus Boswellia, which includes B. carterii,
B. serrata, B. sacra, and many others.

Frankincense was burnt by the Egyptians and is used as an incense in traditional
ceremonies of various cultures. It has a long history of use.

CHARACTERISTICS
The composition of the essential oil can vary depending on the species. Alpha-pinene,
limonene, and alpha-thujene are the main constituents in B. carterii essential oil.

Frankincense essential oil presents antiseptic, astringent, and skin-repairing properties.

It has a resinous, woody, balsamic aroma and is a good choice for products suitable for
mature skin.

Try it with ylang-ylang and bergamot. In general, frankincense blends well with citrus oils,
rose, sandalwood, palmarosa, neroli, and geranium.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in soothing products, emulsions, facial and body skincare, and haircare.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Avoid the use of old or oxidised oils due to the risk of skin sensitisation.
Never use essential oils undiluted.

name: Geranium essential oil
function: Fragrance, perfuming Fragrance family                         Floral, green
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Geranium essential oil has a rose-like odour and is extensively used in perfumery,
aromatherapy, cosmetics, food, and pharmaceutical industries.

Its aroma can vary depending on the species variety and the plant growing conditions.

CHARACTERISTICS
Citronellol, geraniol, and linalool are the major components of geranium essential oil.

Geranium essential oil presents antibacterial and antifungal properties, as well as
astringent effects. It also helps to reduce skin inflammation and irritation. Because it
helps cleanse oily complexions, it is often a good choice for acne-prone skin.

It has an intense, floral aroma and is recommended for use in small amounts due to its
strong scent.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
This essential oil is a good choice for formulations directed to mature and problem skin.

Try it with other floral essential oils such as lavender and balance it with citrus oils. In
general, geranium blends well with citrus oils, bergamot, rose, clary sage, palmarosa,
rosemary and ylang-ylang.

Use it in facial and body skincare as well as haircare.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Geranium essential oil contains geraniol, which has dermal limits regulated by IFRA.
Please see the Essential Oil Dermal Limits Guide for more information.

Never use essential oils undiluted.

name: Grapefruit essential oil
function: Fragrance, perfuming Fragrance family                         Citrus, fruity
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Grapefruit essential oil has a lovely and uplifting citrus aroma. D-limonene, beta-myrcene,
and alpha-pinene are major components of this oil. It presents antibacterial and antifungal
effects and also helps with cellulitis and localised fat treatment. Grapefruit essential oil is
generally recognised as safe (GRAS).

CHARACTERISTICS
It has a bright, refreshing and energising citrus aroma. It is a good choice for body
skincare products, especially for firming, anti-cellulite formulations. Likewise, it also works
well in other products such as shower gels and body lotions.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Try it with other citrus oils, such as sweet orange. It also works well with some floral and
woody oils. To combat cellulite, combine it with fennel essential oil. Grapefruit blends well
with other citrus oils, such as sweet orange, and makes good combinations with floral
aromas like geranium, lavender, and palmarosa. You can also try mixing it with woody oils or
peppermint, rosemary, patchouli and frankincense.

Use it in facial and body skincare and haircare.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Grapefruit essential oil is phototoxic (dermal limit of 4% for leave-on products). It can
cause skin sensitisation if oxidised. To avoid oxidation, store grapefruit essential oil in
dark, airtight containers, protected from heat. Never use essential oils undiluted.

name: Helichrysum essential oil
function: Fragrance, perfuming Fragrance family                          Herbaceous, green
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Helichrysum, also known as immortelle or everlasting, has a rich, pungent, and sweet
herbaceous aroma. This essential oil possesses antibacterial, antifungal, and anti-
inflammatory properties. It has been studied for its role in the skin recovery process.

Immortelle essential oil is generally recognised as safe (GRAS).

CHARACTERISTICS
Its main constituents are neryl acetate, gamma-curcumene and alpha-pinene.

Its aroma is very heady, earthy, and floral. It is a good choice for anti-ageing products,
in formulas for rejuvenation and reducing wrinkles.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Try it with geranium, carrot, lavender, or citrus oils. In general, helichrysum blends well with
citrus oils, clary sage, frankincense, sandalwood, and rose.

Use it in facial and body skincare.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It has a strong aroma. Never use essential oils undiluted.

name: Juniper berry essential oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Juniper berry essential oil has a refreshing sweet-balsamic, woody-green aroma. It is
actually being studied for its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and skin-repairing properties.
It also works well in products for oily and acne-prone skin because it helps to balance
sebum production.

CHARACTERISTICS
The main components of juniper berry essential oil are alpha-pinene, delta-3-carene and
limonene.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Its uplifting fragrance blends well with citrus and spice essential oils.

Use it in facial and body skincare.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Never use essential oils undiluted.

name: Lavender essential oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Lavender essential oil has a renowned aroma and is widely used in cosmetics for
fragrance purposes. It has moderate antioxidant, antiseptic and anti-inflammatory effects.

CHARACTERISTICS
Lavender oil has been reported to contain more than a hundred components, with linalool,
linalyl acetate, lavandulyl acetate, camphor and 1,8-cineole being the predominant ones.

Its floral aroma makes it a favourite among many formulators. It is easy to use as it
blends well with many other oils. It is frequently used in nighttime products, as it is known
to help ease stress and aid sleeping.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Try it with sweet orange and manuka. Add it to haircare products with peppermint or
rosemary. In general, lavender blends well with citrus oils and other florals such as geranium
and rose. Try it also with neroli, chamomile, palmarosa, lemongrass, patchouli,
and rosemary.

Use it in facial and body skincare and haircare.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Never use essential oils undiluted.

name: Lemon essential oil
function: Fragrance, skin conditioning, perfuming Fragrance family                         Citrus, fruity
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Lemon has an uplifting fragrance and also presents antimicrobial and antioxidant activity.

CHARACTERISTICS
Lemon essential oil's main constituents are D-limonene, beta-pinene, and gamma-
terpinene. The expressed essential oil contains furanocoumarins.

This essential oil has a zesty, citrusy aroma. It is often added to formulas that aim to
reduce cellulite, as it helps improve microcirculation. Lemon oil also works in anti-ageing
products and products designed for oily skin.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Try it with sweet orange and frankincense. Add it to haircare products to combat greasy
hair, or use it in shower products for a refreshing start to the day. In general, lemon blends
well with other citrus oils, florals such as geranium and rose, and also neroli, chamomile,
palmarosa, lemongrass, patchouli, and rosemary. Use it in facial and body skincare
and haircare.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Lemon essential oil can be phototoxic. Limonene is considered an allergen, and its
oxidation products can cause allergic reactions. To avoid oxidation, store lemon essential
oil in dark, airtight containers, protected from heat. Never use essential oils undiluted.

name: Lemon balm essential oil
function: Fragrance, tonic, perfuming Fragrance family                         Herbal, lemony
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Lemon balm, also known as Melissa or sweet balm, has been used by European herbalists
since the Middle Ages. Lemon balm is mentioned in many old pharmacopoeias. It was
also the key ingredient in Carmelite water, a popular herbal tonic in 17th century Europe
that was valued as a “miracle water”.

Lemon balm is an expensive essential oil. It is steam distilled from the flowering tops,
leaves and stems, although the upper parts of the plant contain more oil. The main reason
for its high cost is down to the fact that the yields are low – around 0.5 mL of essential
oil per kilo of lemon balm distilled. That is why you will often find lemon balm essential
oil mixed with other citrus fragrances, such as lemongrass or citronella. In other words,
beware of counterfeit oils.

CHARACTERISTICS
The main components of lemon balm oil are geranial, neral, and beta-caryophyllene.
This oil presents some antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in facial products for inflamed and acne-prone skin.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Never use essential oils undiluted.

name: Myrrh essential oil
function: Fragrance, skin conditioning, tonic Fragrance family                          Resinous
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Myrrh is a gum resin extracted from small trees from the Commiphora genus, native to
Somalia, Arabia, and Yemen. The gum is most commonly harvested from the species
Commiphora myrrha.

It was used by the ancient Egyptians for embalming, as a medicine, and as incense. The
resin has been found in pots placed in burials and tombs. For millennia, it has been known
as a wound healer.

CHARACTERISTICS
The resin is a pale-yellow liquid, which dries into reddish-brown lumps the size of a walnut
from which the oil is distilled.

It is often used as a base note and frequently paired with frankincense, given the historical
connotations of these two oils. It has anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in products aimed at sensitive or mature skin. It is also helpful in formulations for dry
skin on the feet and hands.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Never use essential oils undiluted.

name: Neroli essential oil
function: Fragrance, skin conditioning Fragrance family                          Floral
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Also known as the “Queen of essential oils”, neroli is extracted from the fragrant flower of
the bitter (Seville) orange tree. It has a bitter orange blossom fragrance and is often used
in luxury skincare products.

CHARACTERISTICS
It is one of the most widely used floral oils in perfumery. The soft and delicate scent of
neroli also helps relieve stress and tension.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in facial products to reinvigorate and tone mature skin. It is also beneficial for
sensitive skin.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Never use essential oils undiluted.

name: Palmarosa essential oil
function: Fragrance, skin conditioning, tonic Fragrance family                         Floral, herbal
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
It has a characteristic ‘rose’ fragrance, making it an excellent oil to blend with geranium
and rose (particularly, as rose essential oil contains sensitisers with very low dermal
limits, as regulated by IFRA).

CHARACTERISTICS
It is rich in geraniol and has antimicrobial properties that make it a promising ingredient
for acne-prone skin.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in soothing products for oily and acne-prone skin and deodorants.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Never use essential oils undiluted.

name: Patchouli essential oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Traditionally associated with the 1960s hippie movement, patchouli originates from India,
where it is used in different traditional practices, for example, as perfume, incense, and
insect repellent, and in Ayurvedic medicine.

CHARACTERISTICS
Patchouli has excellent properties for use in skincare. It helps improve acne-prone skin,
has soothing properties, reduces inflammation and is mildly antiseptic.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in products for acne-prone, mature, and dry, chapped skin.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Never use essential oils undiluted.

name: Peppermint essential oil
function: Fragrance, refreshing, tonic, perfuming Fragrance family                         Minty, herbal, green
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Peppermint essential oil has a cool and fresh aroma. This oil provides a cooling and
refreshing sensation to skincare products.

CHARACTERISTICS
Its main constituents are menthol and menthone. Menthol is able to trigger cold-sensitive
receptors on the skin, which are responsible for the cooling sensation this oil provides.
This oil also presents anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, antimicrobial, and analgesic
properties. It is generally recognized as safe (GRAS).

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Try it with sweet orange and frankincense. Add it to haircare products to combat greasy hair,
or use it in shower products for a refreshing start to the day. In general, peppermint blends
well with citrus oils, rosemary, and cedarwood.

Use it in facial and body skincare and haircare.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Never use essential oils undiluted.

name: Petitgrain essential oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Petitgrain essential oil, also known as petitgrain bigarade, is obtained by the steam
distillation of the leaves and green twigs of the bitter orange tree. It is very popular in
perfume-making.

CHARACTERISTICS
Its main constituents are linalyl acetate, linalool, alpha-terpineol, and geranyl acetate.

This essential oil has a green aroma with a touch of orange.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Add it to haircare products to combat greasy hair. Petitgrain oil is also used as a deodorant
and can help relieve excessive perspiration.

In general, petitgrain blends well with citrus oils, geranium, jasmine, and lavender. Try it also
with ylang-ylang and sandalwood.

Use it in facial and body skincare and haircare.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Never use essential oils undiluted.

name: Rose otto essential oil
function: Fragrance, skin conditioning Fragrance family                         Floral
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Rose otto is an expensive, precious oil with a floral fragrance, being one of the most
widely used oils in perfumery.

CHARACTERISTICS
The key constituents of rose otto are citronellol, geraniol, nonadecane, and nerol.

This essential oil has a strong, sweet and floral fragrance that works well for mature and
dry skin. However, its methyl eugenol content makes it highly restricted in skincare –
check the updated dermal limits on IFRA's website.

Rose oil has high antioxidant properties, which make it a good addition to any skincare
product.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Blend it with ylang-ylang, jasmine, and sandalwood, or try it with other florals such as
lavender.

Use it in facial and body skincare and haircare.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Never use essential oils undiluted. Highly restricted, usage limit: 0.02%

name: Rosemary essential oil
function: Fragrance, skin conditioning Fragrance family                          Herbal, camphorous
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Rosemary oil is obtained from the steam distillation of leaves and flowers of the rosemary
shrub. It has a fresh, green, and herbaceous fragrance similar to fresh rosemary.
Rosemary essential oil has a unique aroma and is widely used in perfume or cosmetic
products. It is generally regarded as safe (GRAS).

CHARACTERISTICS
Rosemary oil's key constituents are 1,8-cineole, alpha-pinene, and camphor.

This oil presents antibacterial and antiseptic properties. It is a good ingredient for
products directed to sensitive, inflamed, and oily skin.

It also has antioxidant and astringent properties that make this oil beneficial for ageing
skin. Its fragrance is invigorating and energising.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
It is a great addition to products designed for oily skin, hair, and scalp. You can use it in
shampoos, toners, or hair rinses.

Blend it with lavender and orange, combine it with geranium for oily skin, or grapefruit for
cellulite products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Never use essential oils undiluted.

name: Sweet orange essential oil
function: Fragrance, skin conditioning Fragrance family                          Citrus, fruity
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
The oil is extracted from the peel of the sweet orange, and it blends well with most other
oils. It is popular for its sweet, soft and citrusy fragrance, which can help create a soothing
and relaxing atmosphere.

CHARACTERISTICS
Limonene is the main constituent of sweet orange oil.

It is gentle enough for all skin types, but is particularly beneficial for mature and acne-
prone skin. It helps to brighten the skin and create an uplifting, stress-relieving element to
your products. Unlike many other citrus oils, it is not phototoxic.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
It is especially useful for acne-prone skin due to its antibacterial and astringent properties.
It is also suitable for mature skin.

Use it in facial and body skincare and haircare.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Never use essential oils undiluted.

Limonene is considered an allergen, and its oxidation products can cause allergic
reactions. To avoid oxidation, store sweet orange essential oil in dark, airtight containers,
protected from heat.

name: Tea tree essential oil
function: Antioxidant, perfuming Fragrance family                           Medicinal, woody
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Tea tree oil is an essential oil native to Australia where, for thousands of years, aboriginal
people used the plant as a form of traditional medicine.

Historical records say that Captain Cook gave this name to this tree species when he
observed the British sailors brewing the tree leaves to make tea.

CHARACTERISTICS
The main component of tea tree oil is terpinen-4-ol.

Tea tree oil is well known for its antimicrobial, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and
antifungal properties. It can also accelerate the skin recovery process.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
It is a good addition to foot creams and cuticle oils.

Considering this oil's antibacterial properties, it is suitable for products directed to oily or
acne-prone skin.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Tea tree essential oil has a strong fragrance that may not appeal to all customers.

Never use essential oils undiluted.

name: Yarrow essential oil
function: Anti seborrheic, cleansing, fragrance, refreshing, soothing, tonic, perfuming Fragrance family                         Herbaceous, green
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
The Latin name of yarrow, Achillea millefolium, comes from the ancient Greek myth of
Achilles, who treated his wound with yarrow after a battle.

The oil from noble yarrow (Achillea nobilis), does not contain chamazulene and has a
green colour.

CHARACTERISTICS
This essential oil from Achillea millefolium is rich in chamazulene, which is also found in
blue chamomile essential oil. This compound gives this oil anti-inflammatory and soothing
properties, as well as a dark blue colour.

The oil from Achillea nobilis does not contain chamazulene and has a green colour.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in products for sensitive and acne-prone skin.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It has a strong, pungent herbal aroma. Never use essential oils undiluted.

name: Ylang-ylang essential oil
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
This oil comes from the flowers of the ylang-ylang plant. This tree grows in rainforests in
Asia and South Pacific islands. Ylang-ylang oil is produced through fractional distillation,
which gives different volatile fractions of ylang-ylang oil. Of these, the extra grade is
considered the best. This oil is a valued material for the fragrance industry.

CHARACTERISTICS
Some ylang-ylang's key constituents are germacrene D, trans-caryophyllene, and alpha-
farnesene. It has a heady, exotic, floral aroma and is often used in aromatherapy for
insomnia and fatigue.

This oil has antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties. In skincare, it helps to regulate
sebum production and is suitable for mature skin. It is frequently included in relaxing
massage blends and can also be used in haircare.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Try it with jasmine, or add it to lavender. It also blends well with citrus oils, geranium, and
sandalwood. Use it in facial and body skincare and haircare.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Never use essential oils undiluted. Use it sparingly as it can be very overpowering. Please
see the Essential Oil Dermal Limits Guide for more information regarding ylang-ylang
dermal limits.

name: Rice starch
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Rice starch is a polymeric carbohydrate derived from rice seeds. Like other starches, it
 has many roles in cosmetic formulation. Since it has excellent absorption properties, it is
 frequently used as a viscosity controlling agent, mattifier, and sensory modifier.

 It is found as an odourless, very fine, white powder. It is insoluble in cold water but
 miscible in warm water and with oils. It is non-irritant, non-sensitising, and hypoallergenic.

CHARACTERISTICS
Rice starch can be used in oil-based cleansing balms, hair conditioners, dry shampoos,
 body gels and creams, and baby skincare formulations. It helps reduce the visibility
 of wrinkles, fine lines, and pores and absorbs excessive sebum and oil from the skin,
 delivering a matte finish without drying it. It is a biodegradable replacement for talc.

 If used as a sensory modifier, it provides a smooth, velvety skin feel.

 It suits sensitive skin and helps soothe irritated areas.

 If used at temperatures below 50 ºC, rice starch works as an oil-absorbing and sensory
 modifier agent. When incorporated into the water phase and heated to 70 ºC, it works as a
 gelling and thickening agent.

 When added to deodorants, rice starch helps absorb sweat and reduce unwanted body
 odours.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
It can be added to powdered cosmetics, water- and oil-based formulations, emulsions, and
haircare.

In emulsions, it can be added either to the water or oil phase.

In oil-based formulations, it reduces the greasy feeling of heavy oils.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
When used as a gelling agent, the gum it forms is not very stable and loses water over
time, which could impair its performance.

name: Silica
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Silica, or silicon dioxide, is a natural mineral often found in nature as quartz or sand. It is
 obtained by mining or sand mining and purification of quartz and sold as an odourless,
 white, fine powder. Fumed silica is hydrophilic but not water-soluble. In cosmetics, silica
 can take on many roles and work as a thickening agent, absorbent, anti-caking agent, and
 carrier for other ingredients.

CHARACTERISTICS
Several types of silica are available on the market, but the most commonly used is
 hydrophilic fumed silica, often under the trade name Aerosil 200 (there are other trade
 names, though). This ingredient can play different roles in cosmetics, such as an anti-
 caking agent in powdered formulations, mattifier, and more. Here we highlight three
 of them:

    • Thickening and viscosity-controlling agent for oils, helping increase the viscosity of
      creams, lotions, and oleogels.
    • Sensory modifier, improving the texture, spreadability, and skin feel of moisturisers,
      creams, balms, and serums.
    • In powder or solid shampoos, deodorants, and cleansing balms, it helps absorb the
      excess oil and moisture from the skin and hair.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
It can be included in o/w and w/o emulsions, haircare, anhydrous, and powder formulations.

Add it to the heated oil phase of emulsions to use it as an oil-gelling agent.

Fumed silica is hydrophilic, which means it is wettable but does not dissolve in water. It can
be dispersed in emulsions and has a swelling/gelling effect when mixed with oil.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
The particle size influences the final texture of the formulation, with finely milled silica
rendering a smoother, velvety feel.

Inhaling silica dust can result in irritation of the respiratory tract; therefore, wear a safety
mask when handling it.

name: Tapioca starch
function: Sensory modifier, viscosity-controlling agent, fragrance carrier
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Tapioca starch is extracted from cassava roots and plays many roles in cosmetic
 formulation. The most distinctive is probably its sensory modifier property. When added to
 formulations, it enhances the tactile experience, delivering a dry, smooth touch to them.

 It is found as an odourless white powder, miscible in water, and usually with very fine
 particle size.

CHARACTERISTICS
Tapioca starch is a natural polymer capable of absorbing excess sebum and moisture in
 the skin while also delivering a silky texture to the formulation. It can be incorporated into
 oil-based cleansing balms, creams, powdered cosmetics, and as a replacement for talc.
 Other common roles of this ingredient are in thickening formulations and helping stabilise
 emulsions.

 When used in oil-based formulations, it refines its sensory characteristics and reduces the
 greasy skin feel they may leave.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Can be used in oil-based formulations to modify their texture and sensory profile.

Add it to the cool-down phase in water-based formulations.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Tapioca starch may swell in hot water.

The particle size influences the final texture of the formulation, opt for finer grains rather
than coarser to achieve a more silky, luxurious feel.

name: Rosemary co2 extract
inci: Helianthus Annuus Seed Oil (And) Rosmarinus Officinalis Leaf Extract
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Rosemary CO2 is extracted from the rosemary plant using supercritical carbon dioxide
(CO2) as a solvent. This dark brown viscous liquid has a strong aroma and excellent
antioxidant properties, stronger than vitamin E.

It is used in skincare to prevent the rancidity of carrier oils and butters and also to
increase antioxidant properties in the products.

CHARACTERISTICS
The antioxidant activity and the recommended usage rate depend on the extract’s
carnosic acid and total phenolic diterpenes content. The suppliers can provide this
information.

It is often used in low percentages due to its potency, strong colour and aroma.

Generally, it is sold diluted in a carrier oil such as sunflower oil to ease dosage.

It frequently comes with Kosher and/or Halal certification. Check this with your supplier
if it is of importance to you.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in any formulation that contains oils and butters, or other raw materials prone
to oxidation.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It can impart a strong colour and scent to the formulation, so use it in small amounts.

name: Vitamin e
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
It is a powerful antioxidant used in formulations to prolong the shelf life of carrier oils
and butters. Vitamin E protects the tissue from free radical damage and is a great anti-
ageing addition to any skincare product.

CHARACTERISTICS
Vitamin E is, in fact, a large group of 8 lipophilic molecules with a similar structure: alpha,
beta, gamma and delta-tocopherol and alpha, beta, gamma and delta-tocotrienol. They
are found naturally in some vegetable oils. Alpha-tocopherol is the most biologically
active form, while gamma-tocopherol is the best option to protect the formulation from
oxidation. Suppliers can provide you with isolated or mixed tocopherols.

Vitamin E is often available in diluted forms at various concentrations, such as 50% or
70%, typically mixed with sunflower seed oil, soybean oil, or wheat germ oil. Since vitamin
E is naturally a viscous and sticky liquid that can be challenging to handle, diluting it in
these plant oils makes it more manageable and easier to incorporate into formulations.

The vitamin E molecules can have different 3D organizations, with natural tocopherols
having a D conformation and the synthetic versions having a DL conformation. That
may seem complicated to understand, but what it is important to note is that, while DL
(synthetic) versions may act as antioxidants to protect the formulation, they are not as
biologically active as the D (natural) versions.

Synthetically derived esters such as tocopheryl acetate are more stable to degradation.
Tocopheryl acetate is only activated when applied topically, providing antioxidant benefits
for the skin and does not protect the formulation against oxidation.

You can certainly use both vitamin E and rosemary CO2 in your formulations.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in any formulation that contains oils and butters, or other ingredients prone to oxidation.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Higher amounts can make your product slightly sticky and will not necessarily provide
more benefits.

name: Dermosoft 1388 eco
inci: Aqua (and) Glycerin (and) Sodium Levulinate (and) Sodium Anisate
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Dermosoft® 1388 eco is a liquid and clear water-soluble preservative.

CHARACTERISTICS
It has broad-spectrum activity in water-based products. However, it may be weak against
yeast in emulsions, so it is advisable to include a co-preservative that is effective against
yeast, or use a preservative booster such as Dermofeel GMCY to boost the efficacy of
Dermosoft® 1388.

This preservative does not affect the scent of products.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in water-based products, surfactant-based products, and emulsions like lotions, hair
conditioners, body butters, creams, and facial moisturisers.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Overdosage or pH shifts may cause an irreversible crystallization in the formulation.

name: Euxyl k 903
inci: Benzyl Alcohol (and) Benzoic Acid (and) Dehydroacetic Acid (and) Tocopherol
optimalPh: 3 to 6, with better efficacy at lower pH
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Euxyl K903 is a liquid preservative with strong broad-spectrum activity on bacteria, yeast,
and moulds.

CHARACTERISTICS
It is fully effective in both anionic and cationic systems, and, according to the manufacturer,
Euxyl K 903 is particularly effective in non-ionic systems.

It has limited solubility in water, and 100 g of water at 20 °C (68 °F) can dissolve 1.2 g of Euxyl K 903.

Products may develop an almond-like scent over time due to the oxidation of benzyl alcohol.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Euxyl K 903 is suitable for both leave-on and rinse-off products, such as emulsions, shampoos,
body washes and conditioners.

However, the manufacturer states that “due to the restriction of dehydroacetic acid in aerosol
dispensers according to EU-Cosmetics Regulation, the use of euxyl® K 903 is prohibited for
this use in Europe. In other spray applications where a droplet size comparable to aerosol
dispensers is reached, the use of euxyl® K 903 is not recommended.”

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
You might need a solubiliser to incorporate this preservative in aqueous products,
considering it has limited solubility in water.

name: Geogard 221
optimalPh: 3 to 6, with better efficacy at lower pH
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Geogard®221 is a preservative blend with broad-spectrum activity.

CHARACTERISTICS
• This preservative is soluble in water.
   • It works in a wide pH range; however, its solubility in water decreases at low pH.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Add it to water-based formulations at room temperature or to the cool-down phase of
formulations, below 40 °C (104 °F).

This preservative can be used in water-based formulations such as toners, micellar waters,
gels, and others.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
When added to water-based formulations, it may cause the pH to drop, affecting its
own solubility. To fix this, simply readjust the pH back to around 5 or combine it with
a solubiliser if the formulation requires a lower pH. Once the pH is corrected, the
preservative will start to dissolve properly. You will need to mix it gently until it fully
dissolves, which can take a few minutes. If needed, you can let it sit for a while and then
mix it again.

There are other preservatives on the market with the same INCI name as Geogard® 221,
and some might even have similar names like "Preservative 221". However, these are not
always the same product and may not dissolve in the same way. If you're ever in doubt,
make sure to confirm with your supplier that you're getting the original Geogard® 221.

name: Preservative eco
inci: Benzyl Alcohol (and) Salicylic Acid (and) Glycerin (and) Sorbic Acid
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Preservative Eco is a blend of benzyl alcohol, salicylic acid, sorbic acid, and glycerine.
It offers broad-spectrum protection in a wide range of products against bacteria, yeast,
and moulds.

CHARACTERISTICS
This preservative is only slightly water-soluble, so it may need a solubiliser in water-based
products. It is compatible with most ingredients.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in facial, body, and haircare products.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
Products may develop an almond-like scent over time due to the oxidation of benzyl
alcohol.

Salicylic acid should not be used on children under the age of 3.

name: Spectrastat g2 natural (mb)
generalInfo:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Spectrastat G2 Natural (MB) is a natural broad-spectrum preservative, effective against
bacteria, yeast, and moulds. It works on a wide pH range, from 4 to 8.

Spectrastat G2 Natural (MB) replaces Spectrastat G2 (which could be used at 1 to 1.2%).

CHARACTERISTICS
This preservative contains glyceryl caprylate, which is an emollient with antimicrobial
properties, caprylhydroxamic acid (CHA), a chelating agent, and glycerine. This
combination of multifunctional ingredients allows the formulator to use hurdle technology
instead of traditional preservative systems.

During formulation, avoid heating for long periods. It can be added to the water phase at
ambient or hot temperatures, or it can be added to the cool-down phase.

It is oil soluble and has a mild odour.

FORMULATING WITH THIS INGREDIENT
Use it in emulsions, anhydrous products and surfactant systems.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES
It is not compatible with iron-containing ingredients such as most clays. Iron-containing
components could interact with the preservative and produce a mild orange colour or
a colour shift in the product.
